evidence.locator: Supplement A.3.1; Fig. 2b and Extended Data Fig. 3a, b
evidence.statement: Twenty prokaryotic and sixteen eukaryotic references. Randomly select 1,024 coding genes/species except Nanoarchaeum equitans (all 536). Mutate every position from 20 bp upstream to 20 bp downstream of the start-codon first base to all three alternate bases. Evo 2 7B scores 8,192 nt contexts centered on the mutation, averaging original/reverse-complement likelihoods. Average delta likelihood over alternate bases and genes at each relative position. Repeat around stop codons. These profiles have no experimental mutation-effect labels.

Twenty named bacterial/archaeal reference assemblies. Per species sample 5,000 CDS positions and 2,000 positions each from rRNA, tRNA, ncRNA and non-annotated/intergenic bases. CDS: three alternate SNVs and 1 bp deletion; noncoding groups:10 bp deletion. Extend flanks after deletion to preserve 8,192 bp context. Use standard codon table for synonymous/missense/nonsense grouping. Compare likelihood changes, not experimental fitness. The main Figure 2 caption identifies Evo 2 7B; the supplement abbreviates this as Evo 7B.

evidence.locator: Supplement A.3.3; Fig. 2d and Extended Data Fig. 3c
evidence.statement: Sixteen named eukaryotic assemblies. Artificial synonymous/nonsynonymous/premature-stop substitutions and 1 bp CDS frameshift deletions;10 bp deletions in UTRs, introns, intergenic regions and annotated noncoding RNA exons. Species-specific codon tables. Keep 8,192 bp context by extending deletion flanks. Sample up to 200,000 sequences across types and at most 20 mutations per unique region coordinate; summarize median likelihood change by region/mutation type. Primary Figure 2d uses 7B; Extended Data Fig. 3c compares 40B versus 7B across the plotted coding and noncoding classes on the same sequences. Exact per-species/type retained counts are not reported.

evidence.locator: Supplement A.3.4; Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 3f
evidence.statement: Supplement lists five species and tests seven replacement codons (TAA, TAG, TGA, AGG, TCA, AGA, TTA), which are not all stop codons under each genetic code. Random CDS/codon positions, pseudogenes excluded; source minimum length threshold 10 and maximum 200,000 sequences/genome. Evo 2 7B contexts 100–8,192 bp; median mutation likelihood changes per codon/species, z-standardized across seven codons. Ciliate recoding replaces TAA/TAG glutamine codons with randomly selected standard glutamine codons. Supplement names Thalassiosira pseudonana as ciliate-code; main Figure 2e instead identifies Paramecium tetraurelia. This taxon/code discrepancy is retained explicitly.

evidence.locator: Main Fig. 2e caption; Extended Data Fig. 3f caption
evidence.statement: Main Figure 2e reports five species and approximately 4,100 random mutation loci, identifies Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Paramecium tetraurelia, and compares genetic-code-specific mutation likelihoods. Extended Data Fig. 3f describes two ciliate genomes across six context lengths. These descriptions conflict with the supplementary-method attribution of Thalassiosira pseudonana to ciliate nuclear code.

evidence.locator: Supplement A.3.5; Extended Data Fig. 3d, e
evidence.statement: Four named species: human, yeast, Aeropyrum pernix, E. coli. Use previously calculated tRNA-adaptation-index values to separate synonymous substitutions into increased versus decreased tAI. Average model log-likelihood changes across sampled genes/codon positions; rolling five-codon smoothing. Main Extended Data Fig. 3d additionally depicts tAI along first/last 100 codons after z-normalization. tAI is a genomic/codon-usage proxy, not an experimental protein-fitness target. Exact sampled gene/mutation counts and checkpoint size are not specified in this section.

Uniform-random 100 bp needle and DNA haystack; haystack lengths 512–1,048,576 bp in powers of two. Insert needle at 10–90% context depths by 10% increments and exact query copy at suffix. Retrieval strength is mean matching-position categorical-Jacobian magnitude across 100 needle/query positions; success threshold r ≥ 0.8 chosen by manual inspection. Null validation: eight lengths 512–65,536, ten depths 10–100%, 13 independent shuffles, 1,040 scores; maximum 0.037 and reported P < 0.001 at 0.8. This is a perturbation-based repeated-pattern diagnostic on synthetic DNA, not natural-genome retrieval accuracy.

The 57 datasets comprise 52 binary and five multiclass problems. Final-layer embeddings are frozen; mean, maximum or summary-token pooling is followed by a fitted classifier. This is supervised prediction from frozen representations, not a zero-shot prediction protocol. Original splits are kept where clearly defined; DNABERT-2/NT-derived datasets are reshuffled into a stratified random 70:30 partition. The paper specifies fivefold classifier tuning; the released scripts use fourfold tuning.

The supplement maps all 57 renamed datasets to their original sources: seven Genomic Benchmarks datasets, 33 DNABERT-2/NT datasets, eight iPro-WAEL promoter datasets, six Deep4mC datasets, two iDNA-ABF datasets and one iDHS-EL dataset. Labels and dataset variants are not equated across releases solely because their display names resemble one another.

The deposited 1,110,455,538-byte archive contains 57 pairs of classification train/test CSVs, eight QTL VCFs, one pathogenic-variant table and TAD sequences/coordinates. All classification rows, labels, sequence lengths and exact train/test sequence intersections were counted. Whole-archive and per-file hashes are retained. Human individual genomes and expression targets are not included.

GridSearchCV uses cv=4, optimizing AUROC for binary tasks and accuracy for multiclass tasks. This differs from the paper’s fivefold statement. Random forest is the main readout; naïve Bayes and elastic-net logistic regression are alternative fitted readouts. The supplied train/test embeddings are loaded without constructing chromosome partitions.

evidence.locator: Methods: gene-expression dataset and gene-expression prediction benchmark; Table 4
evidence.statement: Whole-blood GTEx v8 personal-expression prediction uses 610 individuals and 21,004 genes at nominal 6 kb context, and 768 genes retained for long context. A separate regressor is fitted per gene. Subjects are split 75:25, with fivefold training CV; MSE and Pearson correlation are measured across people for each gene. Allele representations are averaged. GROVER receives 2,048 bp; long Caduceus receives 131,072 bp, while long HyenaDNA and Enformer receive 196,608 bp.

The implementation chooses 75% of subject columns using seed 42, fits separate random-forest/XGBoost regressors per gene and uses fivefold negative-MSE tuning. It excludes genes with insufficient nonmissing training/test subjects. These are subject splits, not held-out genes or species. Regressed covariates and personal sequences are separate processing steps.

evidence.locator: Methods: genetic-variant datasets and variant-effect quantification benchmark
evidence.statement: Reference/alternate embedding differences feed a fitted random forest, rather than a native zero-shot likelihood score. Three outer chromosome groups rotate as test sets: {3,6,9,12,16,18,19,21}; {2,5,11,14,17,20,22,X}; {1,4,7,8,10,13,15}. Fourfold inner CV is also grouped by chromosome. Final AUROC and Cohen’s d average the three outer tests. The whole-blood Borzoi fine-mapped targets are eQTL, sQTL, intronic-polyadenylation QTL and polyadenylation QTL, each compared with matched negatives.

The classification scripts implement the three outer groups and fourfold GroupKFold inner tuning. QTL generation uses inclusive coordinates from pos−window through pos+window, producing 2×window+1 bases (6,001 or 196,609). Pathogenic generation instead slices [pos−window:pos+window−1], producing 2×window−1 bases (5,999 or 196,607). The paper reports 6,000 or 196,608. Generators exclude chrY, missing chromosomes, boundary failures and allele/reference mismatches as implemented. Released source-table counts are not final scored totals.

evidence.locator: Methods: TAD-region recognition dataset and benchmark
evidence.statement: NT-v2 attentions are averaged across all layers, heads and 1,500 TAD-centered or 1,500 background sequences. The central 400 tokens represent 2,400 bp within each nominal 6 kb input. The analysis compares aggregate attention heatmaps; it does not fit or score a dense boundary predictor or a contact-map regressor.

evidence.locator: analysis/tad_interpret.py; job_scripts/tad_ntv2.py; archive TAD FASTA and BED files
evidence.statement: The released interpretation script subtracts group-averaged attention arrays and plots a heatmap. The archive supplies TAD/background sequences and intervals. No held-out accuracy, AUROC or per-boundary retrieval score is defined for this diagnostic.

Classification: LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42), macro-F1. MIBiG: five-neighbour cosine KNN over binarized comma-separated classes, macro-F1. Clustering: MiniBatchKMeans with cluster count equal to number of reference labels, V-measure on the same cohort. EDS: Pearson correlation with cosine, Manhattan and Euclidean distances; top_corr is the maximum on the evaluation cohort. Pair classification top_ap maximizes AP over the compared distances; it is not validation-selected.
Operon scoring pairs consecutive embeddings and uses labels[:-1], so N released gene rows yield N−1 assessed adjacent pairs. MIBiG mean-pools all embeddings with the same Entry ID.
The evaluator maps Entry to its final row index using a dictionary before joining phylogenetic-distance pairs. Repeated identical Entry IDs therefore do not create extra leaves.

The protein corpus is the first dataset train split, queries are its test split, and fuzz_ratio in the second dataset supplies graded annotation-name relevance. The pinned code calls map on the full qrels Dataset Dict, whose released test split lacks query_id/corpus_id/fuzz_ratio; this is a source interface inconsistency, not a reproduced score.

DART distinguishes likelihood comparison, embedding-distance comparison, frozen CNN probes and LoRA fine-tuning. Trained tasks use validation chr 6/21, test chr 5/10/14/18/20/22, others train; select lowest validation loss. Frozen probe repeats token embeddings by spanned nucleotides, projects to 32 channels, two width 8 convolutions with 32 filters, sum pooling and linear output. LoRA rank 8, alpha 16, dropout 0.05 adapts linear/convolutional layers and classifier. Accessibility is a scalar log-read-count target over the central 1000 bp of 2114 bp input; ChromBPNet profile head is not compared to DNALMs. Quantitative QTL effect correlations use allele differences from sequence-to-activity models trained on reference DNase targets, not a QTL-label-trained model.

Motifs:1,443 HOCOMOCOv12 motifs, 200 positive/control pairs per motif; embedding setting adds matched neutral sequences. Cell identity: five cell lines, DESeq2 logFC>1 and adjusted p<0.001, unique active cell type; zero-shot clustering uses top 5000 per cell, k=50 and 100 runs, scored AMI. Full differential peak counts are 45,184/49,208/33,948/50,783/37,623. caQTL source 219,382 variants is reduced to 6,821 significant+77,999 controls in paper; dsQTL source 28,309 reduced to 560 significant+26,813 controls. These are publication-specific counts before model-missingness and code-specific filters.

African zero-shot filters IsUsed and in_peaks; Yoruba uses var.isused with positive 1/control −1. Probed African counts filter IsUsed plus pval thresholds, with allele2−allele1 for quantitative logFC. Cohort identity differs by scoring path; effect sign and filtering must be declared per protocol.

Frozen gene embeddings feed LayerNorm, dropout and a single linear logit. Train on embedded split labels, select checkpoint/early stop by validation per-genome median AUROC. Final table reports each genome AUROC/AP and printed macro mean/median. Test=False default returns validation predictions; a test flag is required for final test.

Each known operon is one positive candidate, scored by mean pairwise cosine among its gene embeddings. Compare with 10 random contiguous same-length gene windows from the same contig for each of five seeds 1, 12,123, 1234, 12345. The sampler does not explicitly exclude known operons or overlapping positive windows. AUROC/AP per operon/seed, no downstream fit.

All adjacent gene pairs are labeled from the min-to-max indices of each annotated operon. Score is rescaled cosine similarity; opposite-strand pairs forced to zero. Pool contig pairs by strain and report per-strain AUROC/AP plus macro mean/std. Whole 5-strain test cohort, no fitting or training partition.

Separate MLP per antibiotic. Drop missing target/embedding rows; default sample-level 70/10/20 split with stratification for classification when feasible, otherwise ShuffleSplit. Optional groups use GroupShuffleSplit and can fallback to sample-level split. Fit/checkpoint by validation AUROC (binary) or R2(MIC), test only with test after train. Three CLI seeds 1, 2, 3. Binary AUROC/AP/F1/balanced accuracy/accuracy; MIC R2/Pearson, source values are not implicitly log transformed.

Pinned CLI and run default to split=genus, train/validation/test 70/10/20, and CLI seeds 1, 2, 3. Labels are merged with genus metadata; grouped phenotype lists specify target columns. If requested group column is missing, warn and fallback to random. Group-split failures can fallback to sample ShuffleSplit. All traits, including quantitative ones, are categorical; rare classes<50 removed. Test is opt-in; validation checkpoints and per-trait metrics retained.

Zero-shot protein embedding cosine baseline evaluates only test strains, thresholding STRING score/1000 at 0.6. Defaults cap 6000 proteins and 2 million pairs; valid per-genome AUROC/AP and mean/median/std are reported, so full STRING pair count is not automatically the scored count.

Intervention readout uses alternate-minus-reference embedding differences, length change and training-fitted one-hot context/intervention indicators. Five GroupKFold folds hold out whole genes/elements. Ridge alpha=10, LSQR tolerance1e−4; no label-driven hyperparameter search. Report mean within-group Spearman, with whole-group bootstrap.

Atlas tunes a shared ridge penalty on 4,223 training and 1,023 validation source constructs, then refits all 5,246 source constructs. Family separation excludes 27 source constructs linked to 2,411 candidates. Choose 10 candidates for each of 16 on/off-cell requests using predicted minimum on-target minus clipped maximum off-target activity. Candidate assay outcomes are read only after all choices are stored; score gain over intent-matched random selection, separately for two experimental replicates.

GTEx prediction fits 51 ridge outputs on 12,146 genes; select one shared penalty from 10000, 1000,100, 10, 1, 0.1 by 1,350 validation-gene standardized MSE. Features and targets scale on training genes only; no train+validation refit. Rank 51 predicted tissue profiles against 51 observed profiles using Spearman across 5,782 common test genes. Top 1 tissue identity uses fractional ties; whole-gene 10000-draw bootstrap preserves all 51 tissue queries. This tests represented tissue profiles, not unseen tissue transfer.

One central masked nucleotide per 1,200 bp reference window, 512 evaluation windows from separate 1 Mb blocks and 1,024 baseline-training windows. Primary mean negative log 2 true-base probability; no probability clipping. One-query accuracy grants fractional tie credit; multi-query adapters average query losses/accuracy within each window before resampling.

evidence.statement: Complete bundled files inspected: prior panel 1536 rows (1024 baseline training/512 evaluation); Atlas population 7684 rows (4223 train/1023 validation/2411 candidate/27 excluded), source activity 5246 rows and candidate activity 2411 rows with 24 replicate-cell columns; Siraj direct outcomes 181458 IDs; numerical reference 340584 records ×4 columns; GTEx truth 19282 genes ×51 tissues with 12146 train/1350 validation/5786 original test indices. These confirm bundled tables, not a recount of downloaded OpenSplice/Siraj source archives.

Fine classification uses 48 NP Classifier labels, all products unioned within a BGC. The random column holds out fold 4 of the supplied five-fold split, rather than averaging all five folds. Primary AUROC averages classes weighted by positive test examples, excluding classes without both test outcomes. The scorer aligns embeddings and labels before counting train/test.

Chemical regression inner-joins split BGCs with 13 first-product RDKit descriptors, drops incomplete descriptor rows and aligns supplied embeddings. Standardized multi-output ridge alpha 1 predicts descriptors; primary mean Spearman across 13 targets. Raw split-file counts therefore exceed the eligible chemical cohort.

A-domain scoring retains level_b and nonmissing substrate, giving 2,027 domains in 28 classes, not all 2,315 split rows or 2,504 raw domain instances. All five parent-BGC-grouped folds are scored out of fold; GCF holdout has 292 test domains. Every required domain must have an embedding. Primary top 1 accuracy; label tiers are retained rather than equated to experimental validation.

Retrieval scores any associated test product among top 10; four splits include seven class/Hybrid holdouts. Three contrastive-head seeds. Source notes 755 active entries from Streptomyces, not balanced taxa.

The 131-kb cohort has 2386 BGCs and the 66-kb cohort has 2044 BGCs, each with five nearly equal folds. The annotation cohort has 80 BGCs, 16 per fold; all 80 FASTA lengths equal their label-array lengths. There are 2,098,355 positions: 1,685,856 CDS and 412,499 intergenic; sequence lengths are 5068–65044 bp. Annotation metadata uses column split, while pinned CDS probing code expects fold. Arabidopsis TaxID 3702 supplies two annotation BGCs; sequence cohorts also contain Arabidopsis, one Methanosarcina BGC and red algae, so Bacteria/Fungi alone is not the full source taxonomy.

Per-base standard scaling uses training BGCs only; class-balanced logistic regression predicts every nucleotide and reports binary F1, balanced accuracy, MCC and AUROC. The default maximum iterations is 100, overridable by CLI. Code reads metadata[fold], but released annotation metadata has split rather than fold; intended five accession folds are available but require field harmonization before this pinned script can execute.

evidence.locator: Dataset summary, source attribution and structure table
evidence.statement: Original NT data are the 18 configurations used through bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.01.11.523679 v3, superseded during review. Original histones are yeast ChIP-chip; promoter negatives are sampled from source sequences; original enhancers combine strong/weak biological annotations with 6,000 synthetic enhancers and 6,000 synthetic nonenhancers in training. Enhancer types are strong, weak, none. Separate donor/acceptor tasks derive from multi-species Spliceator; splice sites all derives from SpliceFinder. Revised human chromosome holdouts do not establish the original biological split.

evidence.locator: Methods / Nucleotide Transformer downstream tasks, Dataset splits and performance evaluation
evidence.statement: Peer-reviewed revised human tasks use chr 20/21 for test and remaining chromosomes for training, remove Ns, balance negatives and cap training 30000 and testing 3000 rows. Within released training, tenfold 90/10 train/validation checkpoint selection repeatedly evaluates the same chromosome-held-out test. Final per-task score is median MCC across ten runs. Histones are K562 human ChIP-seq, unlike original yeast histone tasks; enhancer types are tissue-specific, invariant, none.

evidence.locator: Pinned original donor/acceptor name fields and official UniProt taxonomy
evidence.statement: Original donor/acceptor sample identifiers contain 126 organism mnemonics across train/test. Exact official mappings confirm named model organisms, including human, mouse, rat, chimpanzee, chicken, zebrafish, fly, worm, Chlamydomonas, cattle, pig, marmoset, silkworm and Tribolium. Presence and per-organism rows are read from each pinned split; this is not human-only or a held-out-species split.

GENERator evaluates original/revised NT, GenomicBenchmarks and GenerTasks using full fine-tuning and a linear task head. Paper reports ten-fold averages and hyperparameter search over nine learning rates and four batch sizes, with early stopping patience 5. Causal models use terminal EOS embedding; masked models use BOS/CLS; all final-layer backbones are trained. P450/histone generation uses approximately 400000 training CDS per family and samples 100000 sequences per temperature/nucleus pair; after translation/training-deduplication, 10000 unique sequences per family are analyzed. These are protein-family-derived coding sequences, not evidence of genome viability.

GENERator-v2 recovery samples 6144-bp RefSeq inputs ending in CDS with at least two-thirds noncoding context and compares the next 30 nt with reference. Runtime uses 30000 inputs and 50-nt outputs, a different workload. Revised NT full fine-tuning uses the 1B model only, truncates to a multiple of six, adds separator <s> at both ends and reads the terminal separator hidden state. Search covers learning rates 1e−5, 2e−5, 5e−5 and batch sizes 32, 64, 128, 256; AdamW, 100 warmup steps, plateau schedule, early stopping patience 5; MCC averaged over ten folds.

Structure-guided insertion design uses CENO proposals and Akita-guided search, then freezes candidates before AlphaGenome evaluation at five positional shifts spanning ±8192 bp. At 4q25: 15312-bp insertions, 160 candidates in five groups of 32; at LMO2: 26629-bp insertions, 136 candidates in four groups of 32 plus eight beam candidates. Beam candidates share search lineages (mean identity 81%/92%), so nominal candidates are not independent trials. At IGF2: 15312-bp insertions, promoter–super-enhancer recovery uses a matched neutral-insertion reference; AlphaGenome averages five shifts but Akita has one evaluation.

Enhancer generator targets Astro, Oligo, Pvalb and Sst with 500-bp outputs conditioned by one prefix byte. SFT retains oracle MinGap ≥5, up to 8000 training/1000 validation examples per cell type and six epochs. GRPO/DAPO uses 32 completions per prompt, temperature 0.9, KL coefficient 0.03 and 300 optimization steps. Generated DNA is center-padded with N to 2114 bp and scored by the same frozen 19-subclass accessibility oracle used for filtering data and training rewards. Retrospective AAV oracle validation does not prospectively validate newly generated sequences.

Mouse cortex accessibility oracle inputs 2114 bp and predicts 19 subclass values. Unfrozen 600 M CENO backbone plus dilated CNN, pooling and linear output; chromosome 8/10 validation, 9/18 test, remaining train. Two-stage consensus then subclass specific peaks; cosine pattern loss plus log1p MSE; Adam, validation plateau and early stop. Report Pearson, Spearman and related regression metrics on held-out regions. Independent retrospective AAV tested mouse/human-liftover enhancers assess cell classes with rank, precision/recall/F1 and NES, not new design candidate activity.

The report lists 8862 binary causal-eQTL examples for human noncoding/coding variants and evaluates likelihood-based variant classification/AUROC. This panel is distinct from GTEx/MPRA eQTL PromoterAI and NTv3 GTEx cohorts. The inspected report does not identify a per-example input manifest, complete causal posterior filter recipe or biological train/test split for this specific fixed zero shot cohort.

evidence.locator: Results / improved cross-species expression and translation prediction; Methods/gene prediction; Fig.5, S15; Table S9
evidence.statement: Journal results include maximum expression across tissues and a separate Arabidopsis-to-maize leaf expression transfer experiment. Maximum expression shares 17-species Andropogoneae training/validation and NAM maize test context; primary leaf expression methods describe log10 TPM and TPM>1 on/off, not a complete maximum expression normalization recipe. Arabidopsis transfer uses separate expression data and 1024 bp upstream/downstream input, with reported AUROC 0.786 within Arabidopsis vs 0.631 in maize. The seven HF fine-tuning configurations do not expose matching named maximum expression or separate Arabidopsis expression-transfer files.

evidence.locator: Methods / nucleotide, exon, CDS and transcript evaluation
evidence.statement: Historical GeneCAD paper reports nucleotide/exon/transcript metrics and a phase-aware CDS evaluator. The current revision uses coding-only GffCompare with distinct default/strict chain settings and does not substitute for historical phase-aware CDS metrics. Per-species reference feature denominators are not enumerated in the historical paper and are not reconstructed from newer revision output tables.

Pseudomonadati is a kingdom in the primary lineage; it is distinct from the phylum Pseudomonadota.

It does not contain the filtered DMS, ncRNA, promoter, essentiality or selected-generation assay tables. It is a code release, rather than Data S1 or an evaluation dataset.

evidence.statement: The paper explicitly releases OpenGenome2 as pretraining data; mouse ATAC reads under PRJNA1314301; human ATAC reads under PRJNA1314272; Supplementary Data 1 human variant-effect result summaries; and Supplementary Data 3 experimentally tested chromatin-design sequences. evidence.locator: All worksheets, all nonblank rows and complete sequence strings
evidence.statement: Workbook contains one worksheet with 705 model-by-cohort result rows: ClinVar 539, SpliceVarDB 46, BRCA1 76 and BRCA2 44. Columns include model, dataset, genomic feature, variant type, subcategory, positive/negative counts, total variants, AUROC and AUPRC. It contains no variant coordinates, mutant DNA sequences or per-variant model scores. Counts depend on the result row and need not match figure captions.

evidence.locator: All worksheets, all nonblank rows and complete sequence strings
evidence.statement: Workbook contains six mouse design sequences (five 19,968-nt sequences and one 19,584-nt sequence), 50 human construct rows plus the pAF0977 plasmid. Human rows comprise 43 short constructs (including three named controls) and seven long constructs. A11 and B1 have identical sequence strings; C6 contains one nonbreaking-space character. Two raw-read construct IDs, E1 and E4, are absent. Human synthesis strings generally include 40 flanking bases in addition to 1,024/4,096 designed bases.

Evo 2 scores mutant-minus-reference log likelihood in a variant-centered 8,192-bp genomic window. Non-SNV windows add/remove edge context to keep scored length equal. More negative changes indicate greater deleteriousness. A.3.13 uses October 2024 nuclear ClinVar with at least two review stars, alleles at most 64 nt and no uncertain-significance labels; A.3.14 removes low-frequency SpliceVarDB labels; A.3.15 binarizes BRCA saturation-editing study classes.

BRCA1 positions are split 1,060 train/266 test out of 1,326 unique positions, retaining all alternate alleles together: 3,104 train and 789 test SNVs. WT/alternate, forward/reverse embeddings are mean pooled around the mutation and concatenated. Ridge regression is selected by five-fold training-only position-group cross-validation: layer 20, pool width 128, alpha 1,000.

Complete upstream Findlay workbook read: 3,893 SNVs across 1,326 positions, FUNC 2,821, INT 249 and LOF 823. This is an actual sequence-variant label resource; Evo 2 scores and original probe split assignments are not columns.

Notebook constructs 8,192-bp hg19 reference/alternate windows for all 3,893 BRCA1 SNVs, computes alternate-minus-reference sequence scores and AUROC. It explicitly runs Evo 2 1B base as a demonstration; it does not reproduce the original 7B/40B results or ridge-probe split.

evidence.locator: A.3.10; Fig. 2j and Extended Data Fig. 3h; PDF page 16
evidence.statement: Original Evo 2 uses binary essentiality from 56 bacterial and two archaeal DEG genomes, plus lambda/P1 CRISPRi binary labels from Piya et al. Each gene receives symmetric context totaling 8,192 bp (first 8,192 bp if the gene is longer), with TAATAATAATAGTGA inserted 12 nt after the gene start. Disrupted-minus-reference likelihood ranks genes and AUROC is calculated separately per genome. Base and context-extended 7B/40B checkpoints are compared.

evidence.locator: A.3.11; Extended Data Fig. 3i; PDF page 16
evidence.statement: DepMap Public 24Q4 ScreenGeneEffect.csv, Gene.csv and AchillesScreenQCReport.csv provide Chronos copy-number-adjusted effects for 1,401 CRISPR screens. Gene effects are averaged across screens and matched to Ensembl 114 GRCh38 CDS, yielding 16,434 protein-coding genes. Inputs are CDS alone, truncated to the first 8,192 bp for longer genes; the reference control is dinucleotide-preserving shuffled CDS. The figure reports AUROC/AUPRC.

evidence.locator: A.3.8 and B.2; Extended Data Fig. 3g; PDF page 15
evidence.statement: Human metabolic-RNA-labelling measurements from Karner et al. are averaged across reported cell lines. Evo 2 7B/40B score full-length mRNA or the longest supported suffix from the transcript end. LOESS corrects sequence scores for transcript length before comparison with measured decay. No fitted sequence-to-decay head is used. The text describes negative correlation; the actual Extended Data Fig. 3g plot axis explicitly identifies Spearman rho. The retained transcript count is not given.

Initial 94 PANTHER 19.0 eukaryotes are partitioned 80/10/10 by species; human/mouse/zebrafish are manually placed in test. Trichomonas vaginalis and Leishmania major are removed for insufficient intron annotations, leaving eight test species. RefSeq annotations downloaded 2024-11-18 include all constitutive/alternative exons. Frozen Evo 2 7B base final-position embeddings from forward/reverse 8,192-bp contexts are concatenated. Layer/hyperparameters are selected on validation species using 150 positions/species; final MLP training uses 1,500 positions/species. The scored endpoint is exon/intron at one supplied midpoint, not a decoded gene structure.

Complete samplePositions.tsv read: 122 labelled positions, 61 exon and 61 intron labels, from the eight named test species. Most species contribute 16 rows; cacao 11 and Selaginella 15. It contains sequences/coordinates and no train/validation split column; it is a demonstration sample, not the full 1,500-position-per-species cohort.

The released notebook loads Evo 2 7B base, block 26, concatenates the final forward/reverse embeddings and applies schmojo/evo2-exon-classifier. It reports AUROC and accuracy at threshold 0.5 on the 122 provided samples. It contains no classifier training or original species-split generator.

Nine prokaryotic and six human DMS studies are reused from the Evo 1 source collection where native nucleotide and protein sequences were provided. All unique nucleotide sequences are scored with their nucleotide-associated fitness values; protein comparators receive their translation when the protein/DNA labels disagree. Stop-codon variants are retained for nucleotide models and omitted for protein models. Absolute Spearman correlation is calculated per assay from autoregressive likelihood or masked pseudolikelihood. No downstream fitness-labelled training, chromosome split or retained row-count manifest is specified for this zero-shot protocol.

Seven ncRNA studies are reused from Evo 1: Kobori and Andreasson ribozymes, Domingo and Guy tRNAs, Hayden and Pitt ribozymes, and Zhang rRNA. Experimental fitness values are compared to autoregressive sequence likelihood or masked pseudolikelihood using absolute Spearman correlation. The method does not report a retained per-study row count or a new downstream train/test partition.

Twelve reference genes in six species: Haloferax volcanii, Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, Arabidopsis thaliana and human. Prompt with 1,000 bp upstream plus the first 500 bp of Haloferax/E. coli/yeast genes or 1,000 bp for the other species. Ten generations per prompt, temperature 0.7, top-k 4. Generated DNA is translated, aligned and scored as percent protein recovery.

Use NC_012920.1 human mitochondrion, 3,000-bp forward or reverse-complement prefix, Evo 2 7B/40B, temperatures 1.0/0.7, top-k 4. More than 250 unique 16-kb sequences are analysed using MitoZ counts, synteny, BLASTn, codon usage and selected AlphaFold 3 complex predictions. Feature labels are temporarily changed to CDS for a synteny renderer; that display conversion is not proof that tRNA/rRNA sequences are coding genes.

Evo 2 40B receives the first 10.5 kb of the Mycoplasma genitalium reference and generates 35 sequences of 580 kb at temperature 1.0/top-k 4. Prodigal, Pfam hmmscan E<0.001, ESMFold pLDDT and DSSP assess predicted genes/protein properties; Evo 1 and natural-genome controls are compared.

Evo 2 40B receives the first 10.5 kb of S. cerevisiae chromosome III and generates 20 sequences of 330 kb at temperature 1.0/top-k 4. GeneMark-S+ProtHint, fungal OrthoDB, Pfam hmmscan, ESMFold, DSSP, Yeast Genome Annotation Pipeline tRNA calls, Promoter 2.0 and tetranucleotide usage analyse components. Natural S. cerevisiae chromosome III/IV and S. pombe chromosome III provide composition controls.

evidence.locator: Complete source table and GEO SOFT series/subseries metadata
evidence.statement: GSE301426 is the SLAM-seq subseries of the cited Karner study, with 10,995 processed source rows and 13 table columns. Its file has one gene identifier and twelve source cell/replicate C/T-ratio measurement columns, rather than a ready-to-use Evo-scored decay cohort. The source GreyHound repository has model code/weights but no processed decay matrix or Evo-specific sequence-score file.

evidence.locator: A.1.1 and Supplementary Table 1; PDF page 6
evidence.statement: Evo 2 uses StripedHyena 2, alternating input-dependent Hyena-SE/MR/LI convolutions and RoPE self-attention with tied embedding/output weights. Paper variants: 40.3B parameters, 50 layers, width 8,192, FFN 22,528, 64 heads; 6.5B, 32 layers, width 4,096, FFN 11,264, 32 heads; 1.1B base, 25 layers, width 1,920, FFN 5,120, 15 heads. The headline 40B/7B names are rounded model-family names.

Autoregressive cross-entropy downweights annotated repetitive bases to 0.1. Outputs are uppercase bases; initial pretraining inputs can retain lowercase repeat information. 40B base trains on 6.6T tokens at 1,024 context plus 2.1T at 8,192; 7B base on 2.1T at 8,192; 1B base on 1T at 8,192. Midtraining extends 7B through 32,768/65,536/131,072/262,144/524,288/1,048,576 contexts with 50B tokens each; 40B uses 131,072/262,144/1,048,576 with 200B tokens each. RoPE combines positional interpolation and tenfold base-frequency increase per doubling. DMS, loss and synthetic categorical-Jacobian needle tests monitor extension; downstream biological evaluations generally use shorter task-specific contexts.

OpenGenome2 contains 8.84 trillion curated nucleotides, distinct from repeated training tokens: 113,379 prokaryotic representative genomes (357B nt), 6.98T eukaryotic genome nt, 854B metagenomic nt, 2.82B organellar nt and 602B functional-window augmentations. It reuses OpenGenome, expands GTDB from 214.1 to 220.0, curates NCBI eukaryotic references downloaded May 31, 2024, organelles, transcripts/ncRNAs and EPDnew promoters. Sequences from viruses infecting eukaryotic hosts are excluded. Random corpus validation samples are specified per data component, rather than a universal downstream chromosome/species exclusion.

Paper specifies byte tokenization at single-nucleotide resolution. Stitch marker # joins sequences of the same species with uncertain distance, while @ joins nearby same-contig/same-strand segments. Transcript augmentation adds upstream sequence and splice overhangs; midtraining stitches much longer genomes and adds uppercase Greengenes-style lineage strings. Conditioning/stitch tokens are loss-masked. This is not a k-mer or BPE tokenizer.

Pinned inference configuration explicitly declares vocab_size=512, hidden_size=8192, num_layers=50, max_seqlen=1048576 and CharLevelTokenizer. Companion 7B/1B configurations declare the paper-matching hidden widths/layer counts and 1,048,576/8,192 maximum sequence lengths.

CharLevelTokenizer encodes UTF-8 text bytes as integer IDs, with eos/eod 0 and pad 1; configured padded vocabulary is 512. Nucleotide text therefore has one token per nucleotide, while phylogenetic tags are multi-character token strings.

evidence.locator: Pinned dataset README and repository inventory
evidence.statement: OpenGenome2 is explicitly the pretraining release and provides component/stage corpus data. These partitions are not original downstream DMS, clinical, annotation or generation scored cohorts.

Original BEND supplies coordinate/partition BED files and matching HDF5 labels where needed, on the ERDA public share. It defines five frozen-embedding supervised tasks plus two whole-cohort unsupervised variant tasks. Dataset files are separate from GitHub implementation code.

The loader extracts reference sequence from BED start:end, applies an explicit flank parameter (default zero), and matches each HDF5 vector by row. Comma-separated BED labels are sparse active class indices converted to multi-hot vectors; a vector of assay labels is not a position axis.

Current pinned config uses GRCh38 for gene finding, enhancer, histone and methylation tasks, and GRCh37.no-chr.fa for accessibility. Gene finding has no extra flank override. BED flank_left/flank_right metadata are not automatically added to extraction coordinates.

When no checkpoint is supplied, test() selects the epoch maximizing the recorded validation metric and loads that checkpoint for test evaluation. The docstring says lowest validation loss, which disagrees with the implemented idxmax validation-metric selection.

The nine-class strand-aware map labels CDS/start codon, introns, donor/acceptor boundaries and noncoding background. UTRs, ordinary exon annotations and stop codons are background in this map; alternative label dictionaries do not establish additional released targets.
For an enhancer cross-validation partition, the current loader uses that partition for test, the next partition (wrapping to the first) for validation, and all remaining partitions for training.

Native SpliceAI2 supplies site, junction and transcript-path interfaces. The public source repository contains no benchmark TSV or per-gene split manifest. The two-model multispecies release and precomputed scores are distinct from the human-only top-transcript and tissue-conditioned experiments.

evidence.locator: Five complete bundled HDF5 model/configuration inspections
evidence.statement: The pinned package contains five distinct 3,131,720-byte Keras HDF5 model files. Each has an embedded model configuration and 206 weight arrays. These are predictor weights, not original benchmark labels or per-example evaluation manifests.

evidence.locator: Role of nucleosomes in splicing; enrichment at novel exons; PDF pages 19–20; Fig. 1G/H and S2E/F
evidence.statement: At one million random intergenic positions at least 100 kb from canonical genes, insert donor/acceptor/branch-point/poly-pyrimidine motifs to define a potential 150-nt exon, then correlate the mean predicted acceptor/donor score with K562 nucleosome signal averaged over 50 nt; stratify GC in 0.02 bins. A second arm relates 14,289 held-out donors and 14,289 acceptors to exon-side/intron-side nucleosome signal. A selected 128-site private cryptic-gain arm compares mean shifted K562/GM12878 profiles against 1,000 matched-size sets of low-score singleton variants, using an empirical p-value. These are model-response/chromatin associations, not measured outcomes of the synthetic motif edits.

evidence.locator: Role of exon and intron lengths in splicing; PDF page 19; Fig. 1F
evidence.statement: Remove first/last test-set exons, leaving 12,637 internal exons from 14,289 intervals. Compare mean acceptor/donor scores from SpliceAI-80nt and SpliceAI-10k versus exon length, with a 2,500-position averaging window. The intron-length arm retains 14,289 intervals. This is a native model-score response diagnostic, not measured outcomes after changing exon or intron length.

evidence.locator: Data and software availability; PDF page 30
evidence.statement: The original paper declares training/testing data, RNA-seq validation results/junctions and precomputed scores at BaseSpace share 5u6ThOblecrh. The current package README links a different score share, otSPW8hnhaZR. Direct requests to both return application HTML, not an exposed benchmark file inventory.

E-MTAB-7351 is titled RNA-seq of 36 individuals with autism spectrum disorder. It is the original LCL RNA-seq deposit named by the SpliceAI paper. Raw sequencing metadata are not a processed validation-label table and do not make 36 patients equivalent to the paper’s 28 assessable-patient denominator.

evidence.locator: Pinned complete file inventory, root README and recorded download responses
evidence.statement: The benchmark release contains GTEx_GTAG.tsv, GTEx_sQTL.tsv and OpenSplice_MPRA.tsv. The root card explicitly calls benchmarks evaluation datasets. Public metadata marks access gated; direct pinned requests for the three TSVs and benchmarks/README.md return 401. The complete inventory has no dominant-transcript, tissue/disease junction, GEL or UKB benchmark table. Precomputed whole-genome prediction files are separate from benchmark truth.

evidence.locator: Acknowledgements and Data and code availability; PDF pages 47–49
evidence.statement: The authors identify GTEx dbGaP phs000424.v9.p2, UK Biobank application 33751 and Genomics England project 754. NGRL variants, RNA-seq and clinical/panel data remain in the secure Genomics England Research Environment under approved researcher/project access. The published GEL validation totals are not a public per-variant benchmark manifest.

Default ratios are 70/15/15. A first split separates 70% training from 30% validation/test; a second halves the latter, reusing the seed. Registered default means SklearnSplitter (unstratified train_test_split), not a preserved source split column. HomologySplitter groups mapped gene names; unmapped names are treated as individual rows. No predefined test column is read by these splitters.

Drop missing selected target labels before splitting. Frozen features feed RidgeCV alphas [0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10] for regression, logistic regression max_iter=5000 for binary tasks, and MultiOutputClassifier of logistic regression for multilabel tasks. RidgeCV fits the training matrix; ValueError fallback is Ridge(solver=sag, alpha=0.001). The library defaults to validation-only reporting; released runners request eval_all_splits=True and separately output train/validation/test scores.

Regression metrics are MSE, Pearson and Spearman. Binary classification reports AUROC and average precision. Multilabel scoring uses micro AUROC and micro average precision across labels, not per-position annotation metrics.

Released example runners use ten seeds [2541,413,411,412,2547,321,421,311,2516,2515], request all-split reporting and pass species=human to build_splitter. This literal species argument also appears in by_embname.py; natural mouse tasks require explicit species-aware mapping to avoid treating this runner as proof of a mouse homology partition.

evidence.locator: Dataset Processing Protocols; Methods / Linear Probing; Tables 1–2; Appendix G
evidence.statement: The paper selects 20 GO terms at depth three per namespace and 20 eCLIP RBPs per cell line. Human/mouse half-life targets are the first principal component of an experiment-by-gene matrix inherited from Saluki, not raw half-life units. Primary results average ten split seeds; multilabel metrics are micro-averaged. The paper describes RidgeCV across training/validation; current executable RidgeCV receives training only. Appendix G holds out weak-Kozak + uAUG combinations in MRL, distinct from random splits.

The native loader declares 31 species/context configurations, reads FASTA header fields separated by | as labels, and preserves train/test plus validation where defined. Targets are binary, scalar regression, multi-label accessibility or multi-output expression. No genomic-position output axis is produced by this loader.

evidence.locator: Methods / Polyadenylation, splicing, lncRNA, promoter/terminator strength, chromatin and tissue expression; In silico mutagenesis
evidence.statement: PGB poly(A) windows are 400 nt with site at 301 and shifted ±1–50 nt negatives (2:1 negatives: positives), testing a sampled chromosome. Splicing uses 398 nt Arabidopsis windows with chr5 test. lncRNA/mRNA sequences under 6000 nt are length/GC matched, with chromosome holdout (wheat 1A/1B/1D). Reporter promoter/terminator strength uses 170 nt constructs in tobacco leaf/maize protoplast assays. Accessibility is ATAC-seq, labels based on central 200 bp overlap in 1000 bp context; whole species-specific chromosomes are held out. Expression uses log2(normalized count+1) and 6000 bp TSS-proximal windows, with BLAST gene-family group splits. Cassava PRO-seq enhancer test is chr 17 and validation chr9.

Cross-assay transfer fits OpenSplice readouts only and removes exact sequence overlaps plus all 23 shared genes from both datasets. COMPASS test contains 4618 mutations in 88 genes; CNN/ResNet OpenSplice training uses 398 genes and validation 45. No COMPASS labels select readouts. AlphaGenome mean-pools inserted bases from final1 bp representations projected to 512 features with fixed ridge alpha 10; sequences are 16,384 bp N-padded inserts without genomic/vector flanks.

Interaction analysis uses 15035 single-mutant and 48054 double-mutant measurements across 110 COMPASS genes. Readouts fit OpenSplice substitutions; exact sequence overlaps are excluded but shared genes are retained. Subtract unchanged-sequence predicted effect, then compare double effect minus both single effects. Spearman is averaged within genes; confidence intervals use 10000 whole-gene bootstrap draws. This differs from the 88-gene strict transfer cohort.

K562 TRIP places one 640 bp reporter at 1196 locations across 23 chromosomes, measuring prime editing, ABE8e-SpG, BE4 max and SpCas9. The model sees8 kb reference genomic context without the reporter. Separate frozen-feature ridge heads use five chromosome-grouped folds, train-only standardization and alpha 1000; a separate alternative selects alpha1–1e9 by three-fold training-chromosome MSE. Score Spearman over pooled held-out predictions;50000 whole-chromosome bootstrap draws do not refit the heads.

MAGE baseline reconstructs both phased chromosome copies for 729 people and 557 chr 22 genes from SNVs. One-hot personal DNA and donor/assay covariates predict expression. Both settings hold out people; the stricter additionally holds out gene regions, grouping overlapping8 kb windows. Shuffle whole genotypes within population and split, then compare average within-gene correlation gains. Gene bootstrap assesses uncertainty. This is a one-hot baseline, not evidence that any indexed gLM was evaluated on personal-genome expression.

Experimental activities measure RNA/plasmid UMI enrichment. The stated selection subtotals do not sum to the reported 12026 library total. Figures compare top/bottom 100 and random 100 subsets; those plotting subsets are not the whole assay library.

2114-bp peak inputs predict central 1000-bp ATAC. Arabidopsis SRX8571616: train chr1/3/5, validation chr2, test chr4 (4646 peaks). Maize SRX21046141: train chr2/3/5/6/7/8/10, validation chr4, test chr1/9 (23220 peaks). Test is peaks only; background is resampled in training. Count totals and basewise profile shape are separate heads/metrics; one fine-tuning seed per model, not an independent replicate distribution.

568 DAP/ampDAP libraries,529 TFs,46 families. Nonoverlapping 250-bp targets require at least 141 bp overlap with 201 bp peaks and 90% canonical DNA. Train chr1–3 293591 windows, validation chr4 74327, test chr5 107851. Full fine-tune 2048-bp input and central 250-bp pooling,46 sigmoids. Three rates × three seeds; selection on mean validation macro AP among settings with all seeds finite.

Maize PlantCAD accessibility: 92cell types,150–128,000 bp context, test chr9/10. Compares full/central-window LoRA and fixed/learned frozen positional pooling. LoRA rank 8 alpha 8, one epoch; effective learning rate was multiplied by gradient accumulation factor, varying with context (Table S11). Context trends are therefore not a pure isolated context-length intervention.

1,251 sequences × 30 masked positions; repeat-weighted corpus pseudo-perplexity. Paired fixed positions, 10,000 sequence bootstrap draws. Nested held-out 131,072-bp contexts score central 8,192 bp positions and symmetrically extend up to 1,048,576 bp; fixed-length training/held-out panels are separate.

Uniform random DNA haystacks; 100-bp keys, 16-bp masked values, 10 depths 0–90%, lengths 1,024–131,072 bp, 8 repeats/cell. One parallel MLM forward pass recovers all value bases; mean base accuracy rescaled from 0.25 chance, clipped below 0. Key/value length ablations are separate linked conditions.

HY5/TCP22/HHO3 motif perturbations: 50 selected peak windows per motif; 3,001 forward passes per locus (3 alternatives × 1,000 positions + reference). Motif-versus-flank standardized attribution, cross-locus consistency and paired Wilcoxon assess model motif behavior, not experimentally measured mutation effects.

Eight BatchTopK SAEs, 8,192 features, k=64; reported dictionary is Botanic1-M layer 35/52. Trained on 80,000 windows of 8,191 bp. Concept analysis uses 32,000 windows from Arabidopsis/rice/tomato/maize with chromosome-disjoint selection 16,510/validation 8,277/test 7,213. Single-feature threshold MCCs are selected on validation and reported on test. PastDB splice tree uses 885 intermediate + 885 constitutive + 885 decoy donors; the report also says balanced accuracy/confusion/thresholds are all computed on these 2,655 sites, so an independent test denominator is not established.

Frozen Evo 2 7B after 262,144-context extension supplies residual activations after block 26. BatchTopK SAE expands 4,096 activations to 32,768 latents with k=64. The mixed SAE trains on one billion shuffled activations from 16,384-nt chunks drawn from 2,752 complete representative GTDB 220 genomes and genic regions of 16 eukaryotic species. The eukaryotic-only SAE uses the same architecture/training recipe with one billion activations from the eukaryotic subset. Adam learning rate 5e-5, batch 16,384, one epoch, five-percent ramp-up/down. Biological labels subsequently guide feature selection, so target-label-free SAE fitting does not make every reported feature evaluation independent of labels.

It does not supply original 100-genome prophage windows, complete region-score tables, the three human mutation-subset manifests, 50,000-promoter coordinates, 50 human feature-selection segments, 1,000 scored genes, or original feature-ablation input/score arrays.

evidence.locator: A.4.3; Extended Data Fig. 7b; PDF page 20
evidence.statement: Contrastive search uses 100-kb windows centered on geNomad prophage annotations in 100 randomly chosen GTDB genomes. Feature 19746 maximizes mean activation difference. Prophage-region mean activations are compared with length-matched non-phage regions from the same genomes, sampled without replacement. Source figure reports AUROC 0.95 on these regional means. Separate E. coli genome-scale tracks use 50-kb chunks and visual denoising; those tracks are not a dense coordinate-accuracy test.

Panel b reports AUROC 0.95 from mean f/19746 activation in annotated prophage versus matched-length non-phage sequences. Panel c separately shows natural E. coli CRISPR locus and three scrambling conditions; it has activation profiles rather than phenotype/annotation-accuracy labels.

evidence.locator: A.4.3; Extended Data Fig. 7c; PDF page 21
evidence.statement: The E. coli CRISPR locus from Fig. 4b is perturbed by independently scrambling spacers, replacing direct repeats with one constant scramble, or replacing direct repeats with different scrambles. f/19746 activation profiles are compared to natural sequence. Spacer scrambling retains activation, while repeat scrambling changes downstream spacer activation. This is a selected-locus internal-feature diagnostic, not an experimental CRISPR-function assay.

evidence.locator: A.4.4; Extended Data Fig. 7e,f; PDF page 21
evidence.statement: E. coli K12 MG1655 NC_000913.3 activations are computed in nonoverlapping 50-kb chunks. RefSeq classes are plus-strand ORF, minus-strand ORF, tRNA, rRNA and intergenic. Intergenic means all bases outside ORF/tRNA/rRNA, not a separately experimentally verified regulatory class. Feature search combines annotation contrast and manual inspection. Final AUROC uses mean activation per supplied annotation region; consecutive intergenic bases are merged into regions.

ORF features 13606 and 15680 have region-mean AUROC 0.99 each; plus-ORF 11734 AUROC 0.87; minus-ORF 24568 AUROC 0.93; intergenic 26069/15481 AUROC 0.94/0.75; tRNA 30262 AUROC 1.00; rRNA 2812 AUROC 0.99. Per-base illustrative tracks do not change the regional aggregation used by these quantitative discrimination panels.

evidence.locator: A.4.5; Extended Data Fig. 7g; PDF page 21
evidence.statement: All E. coli CDS supply features for contrastive secondary-structure search. DSSP applied to AlphaFold DB predicted structures supplies helix/sheet labels. Features are selected by highest mean per-CDS Pearson correlation: alpha helix 28741 and beta sheet 22326. The final plotted AUROC aggregates feature activation over positions of each secondary-structure type per protein. Selected protein/tRNA structural overlays are illustrative, smoothed with a Gaussian width-ten kernel.

Printed AUROC 0.97 for alpha-helix feature 28741 and 0.92 for beta-sheet feature 22326. The caption defines these from mean activations of positions annotated as a structure type per protein, rather than a per-residue confusion matrix.

evidence.locator: A.4.6; Extended Data Fig. 8a,b; PDF page 21
evidence.statement: The eukaryotic-only SAE is searched using 100 artificial human coding-mutation loci in 8,192-bp windows. Top-20 features for frameshift and premature-stop responses are intersected, then top synonymous/nonsynonymous responders excluded. Three features remain and 24278 is manually selected. A separate 100-sequence subset supplies response profiles and a separate 500-sequence subset supplies precision/recall/F1. Any nonzero feature activation within 100 bp after a mutation is treated as a positive response. These labels are synthetic mutation types, not experimental loss-of-function phenotypes.

f/24278 is evaluated separately for frameshift, premature stop, nonsynonymous and synonymous changes. F1/precision/recall are 0.812/0.935/0.718 for frameshift; 0.702/0.919/0.568 for premature stop; 0.264/0.762/0.160 for nonsynonymous; 0.091/0.500/0.050 for synonymous. These are controlled mutation response summaries.

evidence.locator: A.4.7; Extended Data Fig. 8f; Supplementary Data 2; PDF page 22
evidence.statement: Random 50,000 GRCh38 promoter sequences are 1 kb upstream of GENCODE v46 TSSs. Eukaryotic-only SAE features yield up to 10,000 activations above 1e-4 each, with 31-bp centered windows converted to PWMs. TOMTOM v5.5.7 Sandelin–Wasserman q<0.01 defines HOCOMOCO v12 CORE motif matches. SEA defines promoter-enriched motifs against 50,000 randomly chosen genic background regions. HOMER discovers 2,000 motifs each of lengths 8/10/12 on the same promoter set. Reported endpoint is reference-motif recall, not TF occupancy or a dense binding-site predictor; motif matching can yield false positives and multiple latent matches to one motif.

At q=0.01, the plotted SAE recalls 58.4% of all H12CORE motifs and 69.6% of promoter-enriched motifs; HOMER recalls 13.8% and 35.1%, respectively. The plotted denominator is the motif set, not 50,000 promoter sequences or the number of latent activations.

evidence.locator: All 72 pages, all 191 motif blocks and 573 feature-match rows
evidence.statement: Published report has 191 distinct promoter-enriched H12CORE motif IDs, three feature matches per motif (573 rows), and 282 distinct feature IDs. Parsing every listed q-value yields 133 motifs with at least one hit q<0.01, independently reproducing the plotted 69.6% promoter-enriched recall. The report does not contain source promoter coordinates/sequences or the full all-H12CORE result matrix.

evidence.locator: A.4.8; Extended Data Fig. 8c–e; PDF page 22
evidence.statement: Select features from 50 exon-rich 8,192-bp human chromosome 1 segments by top-20 annotation-weighted activation sums and manual consistency inspection. Selection labels for exon starts/ends cover first/last 50 exonic bases. Final precision/recall/F1 is scored at individual bases across 1,000 random genes with at least five exons. CDS and intron use reference annotation masks; exon-start evaluation instead uses first 25 bases of an exon following an intron, and exon-end evaluation uses the last base before an intron. Nonzero activation is the positive prediction. A separate region-mean AUROC analysis averages each feature over CDS, intron and boundary loci. No gene-chain/isoform decoder is constructed.

Features 15680 CDS, 28339 intron, 1050 exon start and 25666 exon end are evaluated at individual bases in panel d. Their F1/precision/recall are 0.403/0.699/0.283; 0.332/0.912/0.203; 0.645/0.692/0.604; 0.438/0.294/0.859, respectively. Separate panel e mean-activation AUROCs are 0.63/0.58/0.80/0.93. These base and region metrics have different aggregation units.

evidence.locator: A.4.9; Extended Data Fig. 7h; PDF page 23

703M-parameter U-Net backbone, 711M with functional head: seven 2-fold pooling stages to 128-bp tokens, a 14-layer global-attention transformer, and seven upsampling stages with skip connections. Eight query/two KV heads, 192-dimensional heads. Single-base vocabulary: 11 tokens during pretraining, expanded to 16 with lowercase soft-masked bases for tracks/annotation. Species conditioning acts only on the functional head; annotation and diffusion are separate adapted checkpoints.

Filtered OpenGenome2 contributes approximately 8T unique nucleotides; sequences under 1 kb and eukaryotic-genome sequences under 32 kb are removed. MLM uses 15% selected positions with 80/10/10 mask/random/unchanged corruption. Pretraining processes 5.6T tokens at mixed 1–8 kb, then seven roughly 50B-token context extensions through 1 Mb. Functional post-training updates the backbone/head at 131,072 bp for 2.5T tokens, then 1,048,576 bp for 1T; only central 37.5% is supervised. A later mixed-length checkpoint samples 16 kb–1 Mb and is selected after 5B tokens on validation accuracy at shorter lengths.

Human/mouse use Borzoi fold 3 test, fold 4 validation and other folds training. Other species use 1-Mb gene-aware intervals, BioMart homology-weighted connectivity and MCL, selecting inflation by modularity and assigning clusters to partitions. Low-homology edges are pruned when needed for Arabidopsis, worm and rice. Training inputs overlap at stride 0.1% of input length; evaluation strides by the central 37.5% so scored centers abut. Track scaling divides by a reported training-split nonzero mean, applies power 0.75 to RNA-seq assays and soft clipping above 10. Test Pearson concatenates all central positions per track, predominantly after log1p, then averages tracks within species/assay; human ATAC is the stated raw-signal exception.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.4.3 protein analyses; Supplementary B.6.2 / Fig. A.7
evidence.statement: Cow/beluga analysis splices CDS, reverse-complements minus-strand genes, trims initial phase/trailing incomplete codons and translates with standard code; proteins shorter than 20 aa excluded. Best same-strand overlapping predicted protein is globally aligned to each reference; identity uses the longer sequence as denominator, scored at exact/95/90/50%. Valid ORF starts with methionine and has no internal stop. Intron-chain match ignores outer coding coordinates but requires every internal splice boundary. Protein analyses cover staged contigs with 99.3% cow/98.9% beluga reference loci, unlike whole-assembly structural scoring.

BUSCO v5.7.1 protein mode, mammalia_odb10 with 9,226 markers, uses the same staged contigs for reference and both callers. Complete single-copy plus duplicated markers determine completeness; unfiltered reference is the ceiling. Cow NTv3/Tiberius/reference completeness: 98.1/97.0/98.9%; beluga:96.0/95.6/97.7%.

One H100 80-GB GPU; whole soft-masked FASTA to written annotation including loading/compilation/inference/decoding/output, excluding repeat masking and evaluation. Single runtime per assembly; seconds/Mb unweighted assembly means, with 13 assemblies having mean contig >1 Mb separated from four fragmented assemblies. NTv3 uses bfloat16 compute with FP32 stored/head weights, central 75% outputs; padding every contig to a whole input raises cost for fragmented assemblies.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.7: gene-level expression and protein abundance in plants; C.9
evidence.statement: Gene expression uses log1p TPM recomputed from AgroNT gene counts and collapsed exon lengths, replacing the original DESeq2 normalization. TSS-centered inputs are 5,888 / 32,000 / 131,072 bp, retaining only genes extractable at all contexts, with homology/MCL-based gene partitions. Ribo-seq StringTie -e -A TPM is a protein-synthesis proxy, not measured protein abundance. All-parameter regression adaptation: Adam 5e-5, batch 16, up to 200,000 updates; validate every 2,000, patience ten, seed 0, best validation checkpoint.

DeepFARM supplies 200-bp binary peak bins; a single peak must cover at least half a bin. NTv3 is evaluated zero-shot with existing species heads, aligned on the same global grid, against released DanQ weights using 1,000-bp context. Matched outputs are 30/97 chicken tracks and 16/80 pig tracks. Primary evaluation requires the entire NTv3 input context inside native held-out intervals; secondary analysis requires only the scored bin. Whole windows must fit within chromosomes; same jointly predictable bins and tracks are used for both models. Per-track auROC uses paired 25-kb block bootstrap. NTv3 saw the same assay/tissue types in different European FAANG studies; this is not an unseen-assay claim. Original peak data are GSE158430 / Ensembl 104.

GRCz11 / Ensembl 116 gene-start anchored 524,288-bp inputs include 163,840 bp upstream, strand correction and a gene-body mask; outputs pool over 196,608 bp from gene start. ZebraHub raw counts aggregate by fine ontology class × stage, producing 304 log1p-CPM pseudobulks over ten stages. Published chromosome gene splits give 18,368 train / 6,110 validation / 7,289 test genes. NTv3 full fine-tuning uses zebrafish token, up to 40 epochs, LR 3e-5, batch 20, best validation checkpoint. Report Pearson across pseudobulks per gene and across genes per pseudobulk. Split-half cell labels with Spearman–Brown correction estimate label reliability, not a model accuracy score.

48 GTEx tissue classification cohorts use chromosomes 3, 6, 9, 12, 16, 18, 19, 21. Score 1-Mb allele-centered inputs using exon-averaged RNA signal over all contained GENCODE genes and matched tissue tracks; max absolute log2FC over tracks/genes, averaged over forward/RC. The full input is used, including positions outside the functional supervised center. Per-tissue auROC/auPRC reduce by tissue-entry weights; 400 tissue-stratified paired bootstraps. AlphaGenome contributes a published aggregate auROC only; no invented tissue/auPRC values. Both single- and mixed-length NTv3 checkpoints are compared at 1 Mb.

evidence.locator: Supplementary Table C.10; complete worksheet inspection
evidence.statement: The 48 tissue rows total 21,241 variant–tissue entries, 10,324 positive and 10,917 control entries. The final aggregate row is not a 49th tissue. Without a site-identity manifest, this total is not asserted to represent 21,241 distinct genomic variant sites.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.8.2 enhancer–gene linking; Supplementary B.7 / Fig. A.21
evidence.statement: K562 ENCODE-rE2G has 10,356 element–gene pairs, 471 positive; 3,826 common scored pairs have 410 positives. Use TSS-centered 1-Mb sequence, native RNA exon objective and input×gradient; score a 2,400-bp enhancer window with Gaussian σ300, missing outside-context pairs zero. No enhancer–gene labels fitted. Report auPRC, auROC and precision at 70% recall in distance bins, alongside inverse-distance baseline; AlphaGenome numbers are published, not re-scored. All-set bins <10 / 10–100 / 100–2,500 kb contain 223/1,597/8,536 pairs and 133/256/82 positives; matched bins 218/1,524/2,084 and 128/240/42 positives.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.9: conditioned sequence generation, data and fine-tuning
evidence.statement: Separate plant-promoter, plant-enhancer and fly-enhancer models adapt the tracks backbone with MDLM and condition embeddings in adaptive layer normalization. Only the 170 / 249-bp candidate insert is corrupted/generated inside a fixed reporter context. All parameters update; AdamW, batch 32, EMA 0.9999; conditions dropped in 10% of examples. Sampling uses 50 steps and classifier-free guidance. An unconditional pass supports guidance but does not constitute an independently evaluated unconditional-generation task. Source-study train/validation/test assignments are retained; no new species/chromosome holdout is claimed for these reporter tasks.

Promoter source sequences are from Arabidopsis, sorghum and maize, each 170 bp, assayed in tobacco leaf and maize protoplast. Outer join on species/gene/sequence permits one or both assay measurements. pPSup Addgene 149416 supplies a 154-bp 35S enhancer and species-specific H3 5′ UTR; full constructs 5,858 / 5,892 bp, padded to 6,016 bp. Conditioning is assay system and five activity bins with cutpoints −2.5 / 0 / 2.5 / 5. Leaf/protoplast host species are not the sequence-origin species.

Enhancer source DNA is 170 bp accessible-chromatin candidates from Arabidopsis/sorghum/maize/tomato, with original source train/validation/test labels. Only four tobacco-leaf channels enter the model: light / dark / 35°C / 10°C; maize-protoplast channel excluded. Modified pPSntF Addgene 256230 has a 35S minimal promoter, maize H3 5′ UTR, fixed 18-bp barcode and EGFP; 5,670-bp construct padded to 5,760 bp. Five activity bins have cutpoints −2 / −1 / 0 / 1. These plant designs have independent activity-oracle/composition assessments, not new wet-lab activity validation.

DeepSTARR provides 484,052 distinct 249-bp Drosophila sequences (402,296 train / 40,570 validation / 41,186 test), each measured in DSCP and RpS12 contexts, giving 968,104 sequence–activity pairs. Each reporter is cropped to 4,096 bp, retaining source partitions; five equal-width activity bins use each promoter’s training range. Only the 249-bp insert is generated. Promoter-selective generation uses the same requested activity in target/background reporters; selectivity comes from context-specific guidance, not a lower background-bin request.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.9: in-silico oracles, sequence realism and D3 comparison; Fig. 6/A.13–A.17
evidence.statement: Independent assay activity predictors assess designs against activity-matched native held-out sequences; DeepSTARR is the fly oracle. GC/k-mer/BLAST comparisons assess composition and novelty. Reported realism CNN uses four stratified folds × five seeds, 25 epochs, Adam 1e-3, no early stopping, with native/native and native/dinucleotide-shuffle controls at matched pool sizes. Also report pooled 4-mer Jensen–Shannon divergence in bits and 6-mer Jensen–Shannon distance, with source-matched shuffle controls. D3 comparison uses its DeepSTARR/EvoAug oracle, opposite held-out halves and five draws, comparing activity-matched NTv3 rather than only uniform-bin sampling. Paired continuous-conditioning fidelity and marginal-conditioning metrics are deliberately not reported because bin-prompted designs do not have equivalent conditioning.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.9: selection and experimental validation; Fig. 6 / A.18
evidence.statement: For activity, select 60 per activity bin×five bins×two reporter contexts = 600 from 1,024 candidates/bin/context. For specificity, select 150 (75/context) from 10,240 generated candidates, plus 100 dual-high designs; compare 150 oracle-selected random uniform-DNA designs (75/context). Selection used the earlier first NTv3 checkpoint; v2 re-scores the designs, rather than generating a fresh v2 experimental cohort. UMI-STARR-seq in Drosophila S2 measures both DSCP/RpS12; require ≥10 input UMIs in every corresponding replicate. Activity is DESeq2 quantified, ordered-bin Spearman computed per reporter; calibration is median oracle minus median measured activity per bin. Specificity uses only valid paired reporter measurements and target/alternative fold change; geometric means and 95% CIs are computed in log2 space. Counts are before quality control.

Single-length versus mixed-length checkpoints use 24 random test genes/species in all 15 functional species (360 genes), above median measured TSS RNA, ≥10 kb TSS spacing and ≤1% N (2% in sheep). Identical 1-Mb TSS-centered inputs: median per-track Pearson(log1p) over 393,216 central bp; cosine similarity of mean-centered input×gradient maps over 49,152 bp; one minus base-2 Jensen–Shannon divergence of head-averaged last-layer TSS attention profiles over 49,152 bp. Attribution objective is log summed RNA over first 2 kb downstream. These measure checkpoint agreement, not independent functional truth or effect causality.

evidence.locator: Methods 4.8.2 multispecies motif discovery / ortholog turnover; Fig. 5j,k
evidence.statement: Sample 1,000 enhancers/species (seed 20260902) from source-specific catalogs: ENCODE v4 dELS / pELS(human/mouse), lifted FlyBase S2 / BG3 state 3, RegAtlas GSE141213 worm, AraENCODE Arabidopsis. All 1,000 sequences are valid; whole 1-Mb context eligibility leaves 989 human / 998 mouse / 963 fly / 948 worm / 948 Arabidopsis. Species ATAC/DNase mean objective → mean-centered gradients → TF-MoDISco-lite 2.4 (1,000-bp crop, 500-bp analysis, maximum 2,000 seqlets) → pooled JASPAR 2026 / TOMTOM-lite p ≤ 1e-3. Broad cores >24 bp separate; CTCF requires p ≤ 1e-8. Output is activating-seqlet group composition, not held-out motif-site accuracy. One 300-bp human–mouse ortholog with 40-bp AP-1 inspection is a separate illustration.

Human HBE1 window hg38 chr11:4,744,107–5,792,683 contains five HS1–HS5 elements. Dinucleotide-shuffle all five, then restore one at a time with five independent shuffled replicates/background-condition. Native K562 CAGE CNhs11250 score is mean per-base log2FC in 384 bp centered at HBE1 TSS 5,269,945; reported per-enhancer means/s.d. Fig. 5d compares five predicted effects with prior measured enhancer activity (Spearman 1.0, P = 0.017). This single locus and its reused native assay context are not a genome-wide held-out linking benchmark.

Inspect 3,792 GTEx Whole Blood variants on hg38 with 1-Mb allele-centered contexts, excluding chromosome-boundary crossings. Three named native GTEx RNA heads supply predicted central signal and nucleotide attributions; local hypothetical A/T/C/G gradients are compared directly. GENCODE v44 and Ensembl VEP are external context labels for selected examples, not NTv3-predicted transcript annotations. No cohort-level independent variant-effect accuracy score is defined for this diagnostic.

Released evaluator exact CDS key is contig/start/end/strand/phase; whole-gene equality compares the entire coding-exon set. Reference filtering removes no-CDS/overlapping-CDS/readthrough/shared-CDS conflicts and same-strand envelope conflicts; predictions below 201 CDS bp and pseudogene-only overlaps away from references are filtered. Decoder imposes phase-aware start/splice/stop grammar and drops internal-stop models. Tutorials separate annotation training, structured decoding and reference evaluation.

Standard causal Transformer (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, GQA); DNA uses nonoverlapping 6-mers inside a hybrid text vocabulary. Base mixture: 70% GENERator-v2 eukaryotic DNA, 16% mRNA, 4% mRNA-splice, 10% prokaryotic OpenGenome2. Training uses 8,192 tokens then 32,768. Prose specifies YaRN inference at 65,536/131,072 tokens for 3B/8B, respectively; Table 5 also reports 3B at 131,072 tokens. Context extrapolation is separate from genomic retrieval performance.

Bidirectional Mamba2 encoder family with 318M/688M/2.1B/3.2B parameters, a nucleotide tokenizer and a 15% masked-position objective. All final base models use 314.6B training tokens in 8,192-token windows (CLS plus 8,191 bases). Source corpus contributes windows from 320 plant species; the context-extended S model is separate from base checkpoints.

14.8B decoder initialized from Qwen3-14B: 40 layers, width 5,120, 40 query heads / 8 KV heads. One DNA/text token stream; 4,096 DNA 6-mers, 1,364 tail tokens and structural markers. Context limit: 40,960 tokens. A roughly 10B-token embedding warm-up precedes 302B full mid-training tokens, then SFT and RL with verifiable rewards.

ClinVar score is log(P(ref)/P(alt)) from the terminal-next-token base marginal. AUROC uses pathogenic label 1; PR area is sklearn auc(recall, precision) over precision_recall_curve, including each region breakdown. This is trapezoidal area, not sklearn average precision.

Global BRCA2 PR area uses trapezoidal auc(recall, precision). TraitGym headline uses per-chromosome average_precision_score, weights by retained classified row count, excludes chromosomes without both classes and renormalizes remaining weights. Global PR area and chromosome-weighted AP are both saved but are different metrics. Reference/alternate full-window likelihood delta is negated for LOF classification.

Complete Carbon Mendelian derivative: 3,380 unique SNVs, 338 positives and 3,042 matched controls across 19 chromosomes. All reference/alternate sequences are 8,192 bp and differ only at position 4,096 with the declared alleles. All variant keys and eight shared label/matching fields match native songlab/TraitGym matched-9 revision 1fde19555fe8c0a55b1382bdf4c6f7082209f566 after key alignment; chromosome sorting changes row order. The derivative adds DNA windows and adapter class strings; LOF here means the causal label, not an experimentally measured loss-of-function assay.

The official public API returned HTTP 401. The released evaluation README names brca2_vep.parquet and reports 6,836 rows, while the Carbon report states 6,840 source measurements; the retained Carbon cohort cannot be independently equated to the original Evo cohort.

The report uses 500 Carbon examples per context, but reports 100 Evo 2 examples at 64k tokens and 60 at 128k. Figure 5 and Table 5 include 3B under a 4× extension to 128k, despite prose describing its 2× extension to 64k.

evidence.statement: The pinned official README identifies exact-match generation as the headline, base accuracy and likelihood preference as auxiliary. It documents Evo 2 samples of 100 at 16–32k and 20 at 64k, differing from report Section 6.5.

DeepSTARR uses dataset-provided Dev_log2_enrichment_scaled and Hk_log2_enrichment_scaled targets with full fine-tuning and MSE. Reported selected runs use validation checkpoint selection, AdamW, zero weight decay, 5% warmup, maximum 512 tokens: DeepSTARR learning rate 2e-5, batch 64,3 epochs, reduce-on-plateau; DREAM learning rate 2e-5, batch 16,1 epoch, cosine; Malinois learning rate 1e-5, batch 256,3 epochs, reduce-on-plateau.

Frozen XGBoost probes use final/default embeddings, with an explicit Evo 2 intermediate-layer exception. Encoders use center-token states for point tasks, whole-window mean for accessibility/PRO-seq; genomic region uses central 100 bp pooling plus RC average. Splice test uses 200,000 training rows and prevalence-matched 100,000 test positions; training signal uses 20,000 training and a 500 positive / 4,500 negative draw. XGBoost max_depth=6, up to 1,000 rounds, early stop 10; encoder PRO-seq/accessibility/splicing eta=0.05, lambda=0. Exact early-stop fitting/dev membership is not enumerated in these methods.

Four PGB tasks use separate full-backbone, LoRA and IA3 adaptation. Hyperparameters are validation grid-searched per task/backbone/regime, then the selected run is retrained on full training data before fixed-test scoring. LoRA rank 8, alpha 8, no dropout modifies both-direction Mamba2 input/output projections; IA3 scales input-projection output and output-projection input; heads are always trained. Classification reports six-species mean AUROC with global versus per-species top-two validation selection; regression reports Pearson/R2 for tobacco/maize contexts. Terminator trains a joint two-context head; promoter and classification tuning are per subtask.

AlphaGenome 2 predicts regulatory activity and variant effects across cell states; Gayoso et al.; bioRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.11.11.765857, version 1 posted 17 November 2026. The author announcement is dated 11 November; report bibliographic date uses the primary preprint metadata.
