evidence.locator: Complete pinned API/research release trees; report Code/Data availability p.53
evidence.statement: AG2 API client and tutorials are public. Report states AG2 model source and weights will be provided upon final publication. The separately pinned alphagenome_research repository implements the original AlphaGenome model and original evaluation examples, not AG2 training or the original AG2 benchmark cohorts. Public atlas outputs are predictions, not labels or original held-out evaluation manifests.

One-hot DNA input (1,048,576×4), human/mouse taxonomy and a 256-dimensional condition embedding; seven-stage convolutional encoder/decoder with U-Net skips, 11 multi-query-attention blocks at 128-bp resolution (8,192 positions), and pair blocks at 2,048 bp. FiLM conditions normalized features throughout the sequence backbone. Reference ontology embeddings or a frozen scRNA autoencoder embedding plus trained adapter supply conditions. Four stages: supervised pretraining, condition refinement, eight-teacher distillation, expression-conditioning post-training. This is supervised sequence-to-function prediction, not autoregressive nucleotide generation.

Pretraining combines the AG1 human/mouse functional-genomics corpus with 36 single-cell studies, CpG methylation across 185 human reference conditions and scRNA/scATAC pseudobulks. Stage-4 encoder/post-training uses 107 million human single-cell expression profiles, including CELLxGENE Discover snapshot 16 March 2026. Sequence-model pretraining excludes disease/perturbed cells; encoder corpus retains disease samples. Fold-1 temporal models hold out datasets published after 1 October 2025, whereas all-folds models use all datasets.

Fourteen supervised heads plus a Stage-4 denoised expression head. RNA/CAGE/accessibility coverage at 1 bp, TF/histone ChIP at 128 bp, contacts at 2,048 bp, scalar gene-expression outputs, five-class per-base splice sites, splice-site usage and donor–acceptor junction counts. Gene masks use known GENCODE annotations; junction inference first thresholds predicted sites (probability≥0.1, up to 512 sites per role/strand). These output types do not establish full isoform recovery or an independently scored dense-annotation task.

All reported core inputs are 1,048,576 bp; interval scoring crops to 196,608 bp while variant and enhancer scores use 1 Mb context. Distillation uses 95% full 1 Mb examples and 5% segment-packed 8–512 kb examples with 1,024 bp isolation gaps and block-diagonal attention. This shorter-context training protocol is not itself a long-context benchmark result.

AlphaGenome benchmarks variant effects using source-specific splicing, polyadenylation and chromatin-QTL datasets; AG2 explicitly inherits selected targets and scorers. Original source datasets and per-model cohort variants/protocols remain distinct.

evidence.locator: Primary abstract and linked official release
evidence.statement: Cerberus evaluates held-out functional-genomics coverage and GTEx v11 eQTL/sQTL/paQTL prediction. Detailed task limits are explicit because full article methods were not retrievable.

evidence.locator: src/alphagenome/models/v2 and tutorials; complete immutable tree
evidence.statement: The released AG2 API accepts DNA/interval, species and reference condition or expression-conditioning embedding; scorer interfaces compare predicted ALT and REF outputs. It supplies inference/scoring interfaces, not all original benchmark preprocessing and label-matching implementations.

Fold-1 teacher predictions are scored on central 196,608-bp held-out targets. Bulk RNA uses protein-coding exonic read-density aggregation; scRNA uses direct scalar gene expression; scATAC averages base-level signal per consensus peak. Per-feature log activity is centered across comparison conditions. Pearson correlation is computed across genes/peaks per condition and averaged; pooled LFC R² measures cross-condition variance explained. ChIP evaluates consensus peaks active in other conditions as negatives, selecting 250 condition-specific peaks per condition for each of 10 TFs and 11 histone marks. This regional/gene aggregation does not evaluate dense annotation or full isoforms.
Figure 2 b caption reports 51 scRNA comparison groups (11 mouse/40 human) and 27 scATAC groups (10 mouse/17 human), rather than per-gene/per-peak example counts.

Conditioning-placement ablations train fold-1 Stage-1 models from scratch, three seeds per configuration, alongside an unconditioned multitask baseline on matched bulk datasets. Supplementary Figure4b reports ENCODE-cell-line and GTEx-tissue expression LFC Pearson and TF/histone consensus-peak AUPRC. These are not the two-stage teacher checkpoints used for the main interval comparisons.

GTEx v11 uses SuSiE SNVs deduplicated per variant–gene–tissue by maximum PIP. TenK10K uses 28 PBMC cell types; IBDverse eQTL Catalogue r8 QTS000045 retains 47 intestinal cell types and 3,524 causal pairs after excluding non-test-chromosome variants used in other QTL validation sets and types with<10 positives. Causality positives PIP>0.9 versus PIP<0.01 controls matched 1:1 on active-regulatory-element overlap stratum and nearest target-TSS distance. Counts: GTEx 67,674 (33,837 positives); TenK10K 12,692 (6,346); IBDverse 7,048 (3,524). Sign/magnitude: GTEx 33,829, TenK10K 6,346, IBDverse 3,524. Sign uses accuracy–recall AUC and tissue/cell-weighted AUROC; magnitude uses weighted Spearman. Bulk scorer sums exonic RNA coverage; scRNA scorer log(CPM_ALT+0.001)−log(CPM_REF+0.001).

TenK10K expression-conditioning uses an independent Gong PBMC dataset, up to one million cells and 25/28 matched cell types; 1/16/128 cells per type with 10 trials assess cell-count sensitivity. IBDverse expression-conditioning uses its own donor-majority-tissue scRNA cells and the same 47 cell types. The scRNA measurement conditions the model; variant-effect labels remain separate.

TenK10K single-cell caQTLs evaluate 24 mapped PBMC cell types on variant test chromosomes. In-peak PIP>0.9 positives:5,116. For causality,4:1 controls are in-peak AF>0.1, nominalP>0.1, absent from credible sets, from a peak with some nominal association; match peak-midpoint distance within cell type without replacement, yielding 25,580 pairs. Coefficient task correlates predicted 1201-bp center-mask log 2 count differences with caQTL slopes over 5,116 positives; cell-type-weighted Spearman.

Unseen Parkinson disease substantia nigra/cingulate cortex cohort is scored natively on T2T-CHM13v2.0. caQTL-ASCA labels require concordant cis-caQTL and within-individual ASCA FDR<0.1:43,526 positive-direction and 43,070 negative-direction instances. eQTL FDR<0.05 overlaps the same variant/cell/region caQTL-ASCA tuple, minimumP per gene/cell/region; 1,620/1,739 remain inside 1 Mb (846 positive/774 negative). Mean cohort scRNA embeddings condition AG2. Both tasks pool instances and report sign accuracy versus magnitude-ranked recall; Scooby comparison has 276 scored eQTLs and treats others as abstentions.

Imputation-split model holds out 184 bulk tracks,181 after RNA strand merging:176 chromatin tracks and 5 gene-expression tracks. Chromatin assays are ATAC, DNase, histone ChIP and TF ChIP. Mean signal at consensus peaks classifies active versus other-condition-only peaks; support-weighted AUPRC uses positive-peak fraction as track weight. Continuous genome-wide Pearson uses 32 bp bins; 1 bp tracks sum-pool,128 bp ChIP repeats with signal-preserving scaling. RNA gene-body aggregation uses quantile-normalized condition-centered LFC Pearson. Scoring includes 1,749 central 196,608 bp fold-5 targets but the model has been trained on sequence throughout the genome.

Nine primary PBMC reference conditions have all bulk tracks withheld and train only on scRNA/scATAC pseudobulks. Candidate rDHSs are ENCODE ENCFF708KEK. Enhancer labels: accessible nonpromoter sites (z-scATAC≥1.67, midpoint≥200 bp from protein-coding/lncRNA TSS), positive if withheld Mint-ChIP H3K27ac z≥1.67. H3K27ac uses rDHS±500 bp signal, not full-gene annotation. AUPRC compares imputed H3K27ac with observed scATAC/cell-line proxies; a separate centered-rDHS signal Pearson tests condition specificity across all nine types.

167 human CELLxGENE evaluation groups compare 5–10 related cell types sharing dataset/tissue/assay/suspension/lineage.147 groups derive from 120 training-split datasets/118 collections; 20 groups derive from 16 datasets/16 collections published after 1 October 2025. These datasets are absent from reference-condition pretraining. The temporal encoder/post-training holds out the latter datasets. Fold-1 sequence model predicts gene-expression LFC from mean cell embeddings versus group-specific 5,000-step fine-tuning of only embeddings/FiLM layers on fold-1 training intervals. The dedicated Evaluation paragraph explicitly reports held-out fold-1 validation intervals, although the surrounding section describes held-out intervals generally.

Held-out SARS-CoV-2 vaccination atlas conditions on post-vaccination CITE-seq cell embeddings pooled over days 11/28. Independent ASAP-seq defines 236,854 consensus 501 bp peaks across level-2 PBMC states. Compare vaccine-induced groupA CD 8 cells versus CD 8 effector-memory; retain 37,035 peaks predicted accessible(CPM≥5 in either state). Correlate observed versus imputed log(CPM+1) differences using Pearson. Selection uses predicted accessibility, not an unfiltered peak population.

The separate scRNA autoencoder is evaluated without DNA input. Denoising uses 16 temporally held-out datasets: average embeddings from 1,2,4,8,16,32,64 cells or all cells; 20 subsampling trials; decode and compare condition-centered gene-expression LFC to full pseudobulk. Integration uses 113,897 vaccination-atlas cells,6 donors,30 level-2 types, comparing 256-dimensional frozen encoder embeddings with a dataset-trained scVI baseline. scib-metrics reports k-means NMI/ARI, cLISI, cell-type silhouette and donor batch silhouette; overall 0.6 biological+0.4 batch, without min–max rescaling.

Gene-centered 1 Mb input; readout is log predicted gene expression using observed bulk RNA or scalar scRNA channels. Score candidate element by mean absolute input-gradient attribution in a 2400 bp Gaussian(σ300) window; no window-wide normalization. Outside±524,288 bp receives zero. Held-out ENCODE-rE2G:4,378 pairs/190 positives across K 562, WTC 11, HCT 116, Jurkat, GM 12878, weighted by direct-effect probability. K 562:10,356/471 originally, minus 3 negative missing-GENCODE genes →10,353/471. Astrocyte:1,902/122; permissive hits(FDR<0.1, negative expression LFC) overlapping cCREs. Astrocyte training includes its 47,577-cell screen pseudobulk; perturbation labels are separate. AUPRC all pairs and distance strata. Expression-conditioned and all-bulk-astrocyte-withheld variants are evaluated separately.

TraitGym complex-traits evaluates 11,400 noncoding variants with 1:9 causal: matched-control ratio. AG2 scores 500 primary single-cell reference conditions, keeping experimentally observed channels. Eight profile modalities use the 1 Mb L2 norm of log1p ALT−REF differences; scalar scRNA expression uses L2 over gene-level log fold changes. Final score is maximum across observed tracks and 9 modalities. AUPRC average precision; optional AG2/GPN-Star ensemble min–max scales each across the benchmark and averages. This score normalization uses the full benchmark score range, not labels.

GWAS atlas analysis uses 6,822,130 common/credible-set SNVs across 510 human conditions. Calls require|expressionLFC|>0.1 and log(predictedCPM+1)>1.5. TenK10K calibration sweeps 112 threshold pairs over 6,362 causal SNVs,1,235,667 unassociated background SNVs and 14,010 on-target triplets across 26 reference conditions. Subsequent analyses compare conservation(phyloP≥2.27, within TSS-distance strata), ENCODE cCRE v4 overlap and maximum GWAS PIP. Select the most enriched condition per trait by Fisher/BH; 17/28 traits pass FDR≤10−7; PIP analyses contain 1,333,700 trait–SNV pairs. LoF burden-direction concordance uses 65 nominated trait–gene pairs,13 non-nearest-gene subset; majority-matched phenotype terms, exact binomial test against 0.5. These are calibration/enrichment/association diagnostics, not new experimentally validated dense annotation labels.

Original AlphaGenome variant test chromosomes are 3,6,9,12,16,18,19,21. GTEx/eQTL Catalogue sQTL dataset is described as 21,514 causal and 21,514 matched negative variant–tissue pairs across 49 tissues. Rare splicing outliers use GTEx FRASER 2/DROP 1.3.3, gnomAD 4 AF<0.1%,≤2 individuals, within 250 bp of aberrant junction; 5,819 positives among>one million rare variants. Chromatin tasks from ChromBPNet include African/European LCL caQTL, Yoruba dsQTL causality/magnitude and microglia/SMC coefficients. AG1 center-mask 501 bp log 2 count difference; GM 12878 DNase, suppressor-macrophageDNase for microglia, left-atriumATAC for SMC. Final paQTL report:613 positive/1,950 candidate negatives,100 matched permutations,400 bp PAS masks, zero for insufficient/missing PAS coverage.

AG2 explicitly reuses AG1 datasets/scorers/metrics for GTEx sQTL causality, rare splicing-outlier causality, five chromatin-QTL coefficient sets, three chromatin-QTL causality sets and paQTL causality. Corresponding reference conditions replace AG1 parallel-head indexing. paQTL final positives by distance threshold 50/100/200/300/500/2,000/10,000 bp are 111/156/202/249/281/407/613; each threshold uses 100 matched-control permutations. SPI 1 bQTL is not listed or plotted for AG2 and no AG2 use is inferred.

evidence.locator: Results: Fine-tuning PlantCAD2 accurately predicts cross-species chromatin accessible regions; Fig.4C–G
evidence.statement: Fig.4D varies 600–4,600-bp inputs in the multispecies ACR experiment evaluated on maize/barley; Fig.4G varies context in maize 92-cell-type prediction. The Arabidopsis-only experiment uses 600-bp windows. The source does not assign the extended-context runs to that arm.

Classification uses 885 intermediate-usage donors, 885 constitutive donors and 885 decoy GT sites (2,655 total). Features/thresholds maximize balanced accuracy. A separate broader panel of 3,254 donors supports activation–PSU Spearman correlation; added donors are excluded from feature/threshold fitting. A chromosome validation/test split is stated, but its separate membership and held-out classification denominator are not supplied.

Frozen XGBoost probes use fixed task-family/pooling settings. TIS/TTS/conservation allow 1,000 rounds with early stopping after 10 non-improving rounds; region classification allows 100 rounds with patience 3. Other probe families retain the stated fixed settings, with encoder/decoder splicing differences.

The harness directly fits LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000,n_jobs=32,random_state=seed) for each of five seeds; it implements no development-set hyperparameter search. Few-shot training samples up to k examples per class from train.

evidence.locator: Methods: NTv3 Benchmark; annotation optimization/checkpoint selection; Borzoi comparison
evidence.statement: NTv3 Benchmark selects the checkpoint maximizing mean validation Pearson, separately by seed, over ten epochs and twenty validation checks per epoch; validation samples up to 1,000 windows. Native annotation models select highest mean gene-level F1 on validation species. Borzoi comparison uses fold4 for selection and fold3 for final evaluation.

evidence.locator: Baseline Models table; pinned full repository tree
evidence.statement: NABench lists Evo-1, Evo2-7B(-base), GENERator, and an AIDO predecessor among its baseline models. It does not release a complete model×assay×arm execution manifest or downstream fitting runner. The AIDO predecessor is not AIDO.DNA2.

evidence.locator: Original Evo 2 manuscript and Supplementary Methods A.3–A.10; catalogue evo-original collection
evidence.statement: The finite original-paper inventory is represented by 83 dataset–target/panel records. Original-paper model associations match that inventory exactly. Other catalogue records are not listed in this inventory; later independent benchmark use is a separate, source-scoped association.

evidence.locator: Per-URL status, revision, SHA-256 and inspection scope
evidence.statement: DeepD DC2, Cerberus/LOAM XML and AlphaGenome2 supplements returned429; Carbon dataset APIs returned401. BaseSpace redirects to Illumina login. Public Synapse entity metadata succeeds, but tested task5 version2 file-handle endpoints return403 anonymously. Five DOI-specific Dataverse requests return403. Official GenBio model index/search expose no AIDO.DNA2 checkpoint in the inspected responses; model repositories retain their inspected revisions. Cerberus release documentation says processed training data are pending.

The logistic pipeline imputes missing values and standardizes features within cross-validation, uses class_weight=balanced and seed42, and tunes ten C values log-spaced from 1e-8 to1 with average_precision scoring and chromosome-grouped GroupKFold. The enclosing rule supplies the outer chromosome split.

Classification uses fixed LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000,n_jobs=-1), wrapped in MultiOutputClassifier for multilabel targets. The implementation fits train and reports validation/test metrics; it does not tune the classification penalty on validation. Regression separately uses RidgeCV, with a fixed Ridge fallback.

evidence.locator: Model Training and Optimization; Post-Prediction Refinement and Validation
evidence.statement: The 2025 GeneCAD paper monitors token/interval F1 on validation windows and explicitly states no early stopping. Optional protein plausibility filtering selects its threshold on validation; no further checkpoint-selection criterion is supplied.

Downstream fine-tuning searches nine learning rates (1e-5 through5e-3) and batch sizes64/128/256/512, with reduce-on-plateau and early-stopping patience5. Paper states tenfold evaluation; released adapters define their own validation split. This does not establish nested hyperparameter tuning.
Genomic-concept features and thresholds are ranked by MCC on validation; the selected feature/threshold is then used for reported annotation diagnostics.
The reference is S.cerevisiae HSX1/Arg-CCU tRNA; combinatorial variants incorporate substitutions observed in close budding-yeast orthologs and are assayed in S.cerevisiae.
The assayed reference is the S.cerevisiae SUP4oc suppressor tRNA, with variant activity measured in yeast.
The target is human FAS/CD95 exon6. The benchmark sequence is the mutated exon, not a whole transcript or chromosome annotation.

The target is the human WT1 exon5 in a minigene with hamster dhfr flanks. RNAGym’s target sequence is the 51-nt exon, so the sequence-origin assignment applies to that exon rather than every minigene component.

evidence.locator: Introduction; aminoacylation substrates and mutant-pool design
evidence.statement: Five ribozymes from three motifs were found by in-vitro selection from sequence space and mutagenized; they are synthetic constructs, not a species-held-out natural panel.

evidence.locator: All287 released rows; unique scores, coordinate offset, reference/alternate alleles; source columnAI
evidence.statement: All287 NABench scores match uniquely to d11/lib.loess.r1 in Findlay Supplementary Table1, maximum absolute error8.9e-16. Every row also matches transcript-strand alleles and one genomic coordinate offset. All are experimentX20. No other numeric column matches all287; neither mean.rna.score nor function.score.mean does. This data comparison identifies the released target; the NABench paper/filename did not name the column.

evidence.locator: Sheet1 row3, columnAI; Supplementary Informationp.5 table legend
evidence.statement: Source columns distinguish day11 (d11), library (lib), LOESS positional-bias correction and biological replicate1 (r1). Mean RNA and mean function scores are separate columns. Data derive from HAP1-Lig4KO selection experiments.

evidence.locator: H3: all native train/dev/test rows; SHA-256 verified against earlier complete-file inspections
evidence.statement: Original NT and GUE H3 have exactly the same complete sequence–label multiset (14,965 rows), but different partitions. The report retains every NT×GUE partition intersection. This establishes dataset–target identity, not an identical train/test procedure.

evidence.locator: H4: all native train/dev/test rows; SHA-256 verified against earlier complete-file inspections
evidence.statement: Original NT and GUE H4 have exactly the same complete sequence–label multiset (14,601 rows), but different partitions. The report retains every NT×GUE partition intersection. This establishes dataset–target identity, not an identical train/test procedure.

evidence.locator: Pinned DART README data links; current entity/version metadata; task5 file-handle responses
evidence.statement: The primary repository links the DART-Eval Synapse project, including raw and processed inputs. Current task5 variant files are version2; anonymous entity metadata succeeds and file-handle access returns403. This access check does not establish identity of current file contents with historical scored cohorts.

Hepatitis delta virus belongs to Ribozyviria. Tobacco ringspot virus satellite RNA is an unclassified RNA satellite, not the helper virus in Riboviria. DQ103524.1 is Azoarcus olearius (historical name Azoarcus sp.BH72), within Pseudomonadota.

evidence.locator: Results: consensus core glmS construct; Methods: RNA library design
evidence.statement: The reference is a consensus bacterial glmS ribozyme core, with designed linkers. This supports bacterial-family relevance, not a sampled natural species or a species-wide cohort.

The reference is a mammalian CPEB3 intronic ribozyme. The source describes this lineage but does not identify a species accession for the 69-nt reference; human origin is not inferred merely from the family name.

evidence.locator: Results: Design of ribozyme libraries; Figure2B–C
evidence.statement: Lib-J1/2 and Lib-P4 fuse the Anopheles gambiae drz-Agam-2-1 ribozyme with a Bacillus subtilis guanine aptamer and randomized connectors. They are engineered chimeras, not natural single-species RNA cohorts.

evidence.locator: Results: Design of ribozyme libraries; Figure2A
evidence.statement: Lib-Tw uses the twister reference described as an environmental DNA sequence, with modified termini and five randomized bases. This source does not identify its organism. Evo’s Kobori panel cites this paper, which also contains cross-species engineered aptazymes; the original panel does not provide a retained-row manifest distinguishing these arms.

The aptazyme library fuses a pistol ribozyme from Alistipes putredinis with the Bacillus subtilis xpt-pbuX guanine aptamer and randomized connecting bases. This is an engineered chimera, not one natural organism.

evidence.locator: Main text: native-locus gene replacement and library design
evidence.statement: The reference is the S.cerevisiae single-copy Arg-CCU tRNA. Mutant strains replace that gene at its native locus; the high-temperature growth assay does not represent multiple species.

evidence.locator: Results: Mapping multi-environment FLs of a tRNA gene
evidence.statement: The reference is S.cerevisiae HSX1/Arg-CCU tRNA, replaced at its native locus and assayed across environments. Environment labels are not distinct species.

evidence.locator: Introduction: reference accession DQ103524.1; Methods: DNA template
evidence.statement: The reference derives from the Azoarcus group-I tRNA intron, accession DQ103524.1. Current GenBank identifies Azoarcus olearius, formerly Azoarcus sp.BH72. The study mutates seven sites and assays in vitro at eight magnesium concentrations; this is reference-RNA origin, not a panel of bacterial organisms.

evidence.locator: Main text: choice of class-II ligase and isolate a4-11
evidence.statement: The reference is the in-vitro-selected class-II ligase isolate a4-11. The experiment mutagenizes and reselects that artificial RNA; its comparison to viral population evolution does not assign it a viral organism.

evidence.locator: Results: Comprehensive analysis of mutational effects; Figures1–5; Methods: library preparation
evidence.statement: The assayed reference is described as a mammalian CPEB3 ribozyme. No species accession is assigned to this 69-nt construct; it is not assumed identical to another CPEB3 assay.

evidence.locator: Results: Comprehensive analysis of mutational effects; Figures1–5; Methods: library preparation
evidence.statement: The reference is a hepatitis delta virus ribozyme. Its lineage is Ribozyviria, not Riboviria; the in-vitro assay is not evidence of a human genomic RNA target.

evidence.locator: Results: Comprehensive analysis of mutational effects; Figures1–5; Methods: library preparation
evidence.statement: The reference is explicitly an Oryza sativa twister ribozyme. A rice-derived RNA mutant assay does not establish genome-wide plant prediction.

evidence.locator: Results: Comprehensive analysis of mutational effects; Figures1–5; Methods: library preparation
evidence.statement: The hairpin reference derives from tobacco ringspot virus satellite RNA. The satellite RNA, helper virus and tobacco host are distinct; the assignment follows the satellite reference.

evidence.locator: Results: Comprehensive analysis of mutational effects; Figures1–5; Methods: library preparation
evidence.statement: The assayed construct is a type-III hammerhead ribozyme. The paper compares it with sTRSV structural data but supplies no organism accession for this exact 45-nt reference; structural comparison alone does not establish its natural taxon.

evidence.locator: Introduction; Results: in-vivo selection of group-I intron variants
evidence.statement: The reference intron is from Tetrahymena thermophila. E.coli is the assay host, not the origin of the mutated intron sequence.

evidence.locator: Main text; Online Methods: construction of HiTS-RAP halting templates; references16–17
evidence.statement: The inputs are mutagenized GFP-binding and NELF-E-binding aptamers from selection studies. They are selected RNA constructs; the GFP or Drosophila protein target does not establish a natural species origin for the aptamer RNA.
The GFP aptamers were selected from a random-core RNA pool and optimized by deletion, substitution and additional SELEX.

The NELF-E aptamer selection starts from a 70-nucleotide randomized region with constant amplification flanks. A separate nascent-genomic-RNA selection is not the origin of this random-library aptamer.
The source explicitly places its 81-nt CPEB3 ribozyme in an intron of the human CPEB3 gene. This human-origin assignment does not equate its cohort with the separate 69-nt CPEB3 assays.

evidence.locator: Results: LINE-1 and OR4K15 ribozyme identification and deep mutational scanning
evidence.statement: The full/mini LINE-1 and OR4K15 references are identified in human genomic sequence. This is reference-sequence origin; in-vitro cleavage does not assess whole-gene or transcript recovery.

evidence.locator: Introduction; Results: evolved polymerase ribozyme and 5TU/t1 components
evidence.statement: The reference is an in-vitro-evolved RNA polymerase ribozyme, including the active 5TU and inactive t1 components. The study does not assign these selected constructs to a natural species.

evidence.locator: Main text: Osa-1-4 reference and library design
evidence.statement: The 54-nt reference is Oryza sativa Osa-1-4; 48 positions are randomized for mutational analysis. The source names rice, rather than an unresolved environmental twister.

evidence.locator: Methods: virus and HA mutant libraries
evidence.statement: The target is A/WSN/1933 (H1N1) influenza hemagglutinin. The sequence assignment follows influenza A, not the mammalian culture host used to measure viral growth.

The assayed 5S rRNA reference is Vibrio proteolyticus. The compensatory construct retains E.coli promoters/terminator and is assayed in an E.coli knockout host; the mutated 5S reference is not E.coli.

evidence.locator: Primary study organism indexing: Azoarcus/enzymology; cited reference group-I intron
evidence.statement: The study identifies the bacterial Azoarcus group-I ribozyme. The genus belongs to Pseudomonadota; no exact species accession for Evo’s retained cohort is inferred from the separate Peri study.

tasks.label_basis: Experimental gene essentiality
tasks.limitations: Original processed gene/label/score tables and exact per-genome retained counts are absent from the inspected release. No new pretraining exclusion is implied.
tasks.input_description: Gene sequence with symmetric flanks to 8,192 nt; fixed stop-rich insertion 12 nt after gene start
tasks.output_description: One essentiality ranking score per supplied coding gene

tasks.name: Human gene essentiality
tasks.description: Average Chronos gene effect across 1,401 CRISPR screens for 16,434 protein-coding genes; score CDS against a dinucleotide-preserving shuffled control.
tasks.label_basis: DepMap Public 24Q4 Chronos screen effects averaged per gene; binary essentiality threshold is not reported in the inspected Evo 2 method/caption.
tasks.limitations: Exact essential/nonessential threshold, retained gene IDs and shuffled-control seeds are not provided by the Evo 2 release.
tasks.input_description: Ensembl 114 GRCh38 coding sequence only; no flanking padding; first 8,192 bp for long CDS
tasks.output_description: Gene-level essentiality ranking against aggregated CRISPR gene effects

tasks.name: mRNA decay rate

tasks.input_description: Full mRNA, or longest model-supported suffix taken from its 3′ end
tasks.output_description: One length-corrected likelihood score per transcript

tasks.name: Exon versus intron positions

tasks.limitations: Eight test species and the 122-position released demonstration are identifiable; full 94-species train/validation assignments, full sampled cohorts and sampling seeds are not released. This is isolated midpoint classification, not dense annotation.

tasks.name: Gene completion
tasks.target: Complete partially supplied genes and recover the reference amino-acid sequence
tasks.description: Twelve reference genes in six species: Haloferax volcanii, Escherichia coli, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Chlamydomonas reinhardtii, Arabidopsis thaliana and human. Prompt with 1,000 bp upstream plus the first 500 bp of Haloferax/E. coli/yeast genes or 1,000 bp for the other species. Ten generations per prompt, temperature 0.7, top-k 4. Generated DNA is translated, aligned and scored as percent protein recovery.
tasks.label_basis: Computational sequence/annotation/folding readouts; no experimental fitness or viability labels
tasks.limitations: Protein sequence identity is a computational reference-recovery endpoint; no cellular gene-function experiment is described.
tasks.input_description: Known gene prefix and upstream genomic context
tasks.output_description: Generated DNA evaluated by reference protein recovery

tasks.name: Mitochondrial-genome generation
tasks.target: Generate human mitochondrial sequences with coherent annotated components and protein complexes
tasks.description: Use NC_012920.1 human mitochondrion, 3,000-bp forward or reverse-complement prefix, Evo 2 7B/40B, temperatures 1.0/0.7, top-k 4. More than 250 unique 16-kb sequences are analysed using MitoZ counts, synteny, BLASTn, codon usage and selected AlphaFold 3 complex predictions. Feature labels are temporarily changed to CDS for a synteny renderer; that display conversion is not proof that tRNA/rRNA sequences are coding genes.
tasks.label_basis: Computational sequence/annotation/folding readouts; no experimental fitness or viability labels
tasks.limitations: All endpoints are computational. Complete scored generation panel and selection manifest are not released; selected folding examples do not estimate mitochondrial viability.
tasks.input_description: 3,000-bp prefix of the forward or reverse human mitochondrial reference
tasks.output_description: Generated mitochondrial DNA; predicted component counts and selected protein-structure consistency

tasks.name: Bacterial-genome generation
tasks.target: Generate bacterial genome-length DNA with plausible coding and protein properties
tasks.description: Evo 2 40B receives the first 10.5 kb of the Mycoplasma genitalium reference and generates 35 sequences of 580 kb at temperature 1.0/top-k 4. Prodigal, Pfam hmmscan E<0.001, ESMFold pLDDT and DSSP assess predicted genes/protein properties; Evo 1 and natural-genome controls are compared.
tasks.label_basis: Computational sequence/annotation/folding readouts; no experimental fitness or viability labels
tasks.limitations: The supplement states a pLDDT filter of 0.2. The exact scale/implementation and full generated-sequence/score panel are not supplied; no viable organism is demonstrated.
tasks.input_description: 10.5-kb prefix of the Mycoplasma genitalium genome
tasks.output_description: Generated genome-length DNA; predicted coding, domain and fold distributions

tasks.name: Yeast-chromosome generation
tasks.target: Generate yeast chromosome-length DNA with plausible coding, RNA and promoter composition
tasks.description: Evo 2 40B receives the first 10.5 kb of S. cerevisiae chromosome III and generates 20 sequences of 330 kb at temperature 1.0/top-k 4. GeneMark-S+ProtHint, fungal OrthoDB, Pfam hmmscan, ESMFold, DSSP, Yeast Genome Annotation Pipeline tRNA calls, Promoter 2.0 and tetranucleotide usage analyse components. Natural S. cerevisiae chromosome III/IV and S. pombe chromosome III provide composition controls.
tasks.label_basis: Computational sequence/annotation/folding readouts; no experimental fitness or viability labels
tasks.limitations: No experimental chromosome function or complete decoded annotation truth is tested. Complete original generation and component-score tables are absent from the inspected release.
tasks.input_description: 10.5-kb prefix of S. cerevisiae chromosome III
tasks.output_description: Generated chromosome-length DNA; predicted feature densities and composition/fold distributions

tasks.name: Guided mouse regulatory design
tasks.target: Design long DNA with a specified mouse chromatin-accessibility pattern
tasks.description: Evo 2 7B proposes 128-bp chunks under beam search with Enformer/Borzoi accessibility guidance, 40,960-bp upstream context at the Hprt locus, temperature 1.0/top-k 4, target length 19,968 bp. Six requested patterns include three square/rectangular waves and ARC/LO/EVO2 Morse patterns. Prediction-defined design AUROC and five-track ensemble agreement assess computational selection; selected constructs are integrated at a single-copy mESC Hprt landing pad and assayed by ATAC-seq.
tasks.label_basis: Specified design pattern, externally predicted accessibility and selected-construct experimental ATAC-seq
tasks.limitations: Oracle-optimized AUROC and experimental ATAC readout are distinct endpoints. Construct sequences and raw ATAC metadata are released; the full sampled-candidate/beam trajectory manifest is not.
tasks.input_description: Native Hprt genomic prefix plus externally specified accessibility pattern
tasks.output_description: Generated DNA; oracle agreement and separate measured ATAC accessibility along selected integrated constructs

tasks.name: Guided human regulatory design
tasks.target: Design DNA with specified shared or cell-type-dependent human chromatin accessibility
tasks.description: Evo 2 7B beam search uses 128-bp chunks, 96 candidates/step, five retained beams, temperature 0.8/top-k 4 and NEBL upstream context. Enformer/Borzoi guide 1-kb/4-kb patterns in HEK293T/K562. Selected designs are integrated at NEBL using hifiDn29-dCas9 and assayed by ATAC-seq after four weeks. Measured coverage is normalized to integrated plasmid-backbone reads; two transfection/electroporation populations are averaged. Main text reports 33/36 within-sequence pattern tests with AUROC>0.8 and 4/24 differential-accessibility designs with >2-fold change.
tasks.label_basis: Specified design pattern, externally predicted accessibility and selected-construct experimental ATAC-seq
tasks.limitations: Generation A.6.8 says 4,996 bp, whereas A.6.9 and released long synthesis strings support 4,096 designed bases plus 40 flanking bases. Raw read metadata includes E1/E4 absent from the sequence workbook; C6 contains whitespace and A11/B1 are duplicate strings.
tasks.input_description: 40,960-bp upstream NEBL context plus requested HEK293T/K562 accessibility pattern
tasks.output_description: Generated DNA; externally predicted and experimentally measured accessibility profiles and cell-line differential activity

tasks.name: Coding-boundary mutation likelihood
tasks.target: Mutation likelihood versus distance from start/stop codon
tasks.description: Twenty prokaryotic and sixteen eukaryotic references. Randomly select 1,024 coding genes/species except Nanoarchaeum equitans (all 536). Mutate every position from 20 bp upstream to 20 bp downstream of the start-codon first base to all three alternate bases. Evo 2 7B scores 8,192 nt contexts centered on the mutation, averaging original/reverse-complement likelihoods. Average delta likelihood over alternate bases and genes at each relative position. Repeat around stop codons. These profiles have no experimental mutation-effect labels.

tasks.description: Supplement lists five species and tests seven replacement codons (TAA, TAG, TGA, AGG, TCA, AGA, TTA), which are not all stop codons under each genetic code. tasks.name: Repeated-pattern retrieval in synthetic DNA
tasks.target: Long-context dependence of query predictions on an earlier exact pattern
tasks.description: Uniform-random 100 bp needle and DNA haystack; haystack lengths 512–1,048,576 bp in powers of two. Insert needle at 10–90% context depths by 10% increments and exact query copy at suffix. Retrieval strength is mean matching-position categorical-Jacobian magnitude across 100 needle/query positions; success threshold r ≥ 0.8 chosen by manual inspection. Null validation: eight lengths 512–65,536, ten depths 10–100%, 13 independent shuffles, 1,040 scores; maximum 0.037 and reported P < 0.001 at 0.8. This is a perturbation-based repeated-pattern diagnostic on synthetic DNA, not natural-genome retrieval accuracy.

categories.name: Plant breeding
categories.definition: Prioritize trait-associated genes and alleles for plant breeding and validation.

categories.name: Variant interpretation
categories.definition: Prioritize human disease-associated variants and assess molecular consequences.

categories.name: Genetic target discovery
categories.definition: Connect trait-associated variants to genes and molecular mechanisms.

categories.name: Regulatory-sequence engineering
categories.definition: Predict or select regulatory sequences for desired activity in a specified host or cell context.

categories.name: Gene-therapy research
categories.definition: Evaluate sequence components and edits relevant to controlled expression in target cells.

categories.name: RNA engineering
categories.definition: Predict or select RNA translation, stability, binding, localization and molecular function.

categories.name: Strain engineering
categories.definition: Predict gene function and cellular phenotypes relevant to microbial strain modification.

categories.name: Natural-product discovery
categories.definition: Connect biosynthetic sequences to products, chemical properties and substrates.

categories.name: Protein engineering
categories.definition: Predict experimental consequences of coding variants and enzyme function.

categories.name: Microbial genomics
categories.definition: Interpret microbial genes, genomes and mobile elements.

categories.name: Genome annotation
categories.definition: Locate and classify functional genomic elements.

categories.name: Comparative genomics
categories.definition: Characterize homology, evolutionary relationships and sequence constraint.

categories.name: Model development
categories.definition: Measure sequence modeling, representation or computational properties.

categories.name: Functional prediction
categories.definition: Predict an experimentally measured or annotated property from sequence.
categories.accommodation: A task-specific output/readout and appropriate label supervision or score are needed.

categories.name: Variant-effect prediction
categories.definition: Score the consequence of a specified sequence change.
categories.accommodation: Allele comparison, mutation localization and a declared scoring function are required.

categories.name: Sequence modeling
categories.definition: Predict sequence probabilities, held-out bases or natural continuations.
categories.accommodation: A nucleotide/token probability interface with an explicit token-to-base scoring rule is required.

categories.name: Dense annotation
categories.definition: Annotate biological features across sequence using position-aligned labels, detected elements or decoded structures. The Scored output field distinguishes bases, individual elements and complete chains; a supplied midpoint label or a proteome completeness statistic is insufficient.
categories.accommodation: Position-preserving representations and a localized output head are required.

categories.name: Sequence retrieval
categories.definition: Rank related sequences or cross-modal matches.
categories.accommodation: Comparable embeddings or a retrieval score and query/gallery protocol are required.

categories.name: Generation
categories.definition: Produce nucleotide sequence by sampling, completion or sequence optimization. This parent category includes conditional and unconditional generation; candidate selection and probability-only scoring are separate.
categories.accommodation: A generative decoder, sampling or completion procedure is required.

categories.name: Conditional generation
categories.definition: Generate sequence with a specified prefix, activity or organism condition.
categories.accommodation: A mechanism for prefix or attribute conditioning and a declared sampling procedure is required.

categories.name: Sequence selection
categories.definition: Choose candidates for a specified measured response.
categories.accommodation: An effect predictor and a selection objective/budget are required; a generative model is not necessary.

categories.name: Long-context evaluation
categories.definition: Explicitly evaluate context length, distal dependencies or retrieval over extended inputs.
categories.accommodation: Record input span and intervention; long input alone does not establish a long-range biological dependency.

categories.name: Context-specific prediction
categories.definition: Predict dependence on tissue, cell state, genetic background or assay host.
categories.accommodation: A context input or context-specific heads/readouts and matched labels are required.

categories.name: Genetic interactions
categories.definition: Predict non-additive effects or dependence on another allele.
categories.accommodation: Joint mutation/background modeling and an interaction-specific endpoint are required.

categories.name: Evolutionary inference
categories.definition: Predict constraint, evolutionary relationships or functional enrichment.
categories.accommodation: Record alignments, trees and population information available to the model.

categories.name: Structure prediction
categories.definition: Predict secondary or tertiary molecular structure.
categories.accommodation: A structure/contact output and an explicit structure metric are required.

categories.name: Genes / gene bodies
categories.definition: Gene-level sequence or gene-body context. Does not by itself establish full gene-structure recovery.

categories.name: Coding sequence
categories.definition: Protein-coding sequence, including synonymous and nonsynonymous variants.

categories.name: Exons
categories.definition: Exonic sequence, intervals or labels. Correct exon classification/detection does not establish a complete transcript chain.

categories.name: Introns
categories.definition: Intronic sequence, intervals or labels. Supplied intron windows and recovered intron chains are different evaluations.

categories.name: Splice sites
categories.definition: Donor/acceptor boundary identities or local splice-region effects. Junction pairing and complete isoforms are separate features.

categories.name: 5′ UTR
categories.definition: Untranslated sequence upstream of the translated CDS.

categories.name: 3′ UTR
categories.definition: Untranslated sequence downstream of the translated CDS.

categories.name: Noncoding RNA (broad)
categories.definition: Non-protein-coding RNA without a narrower universal class. Broad ncRNA assignments are not automatically “other than lncRNA/rRNA/tRNA”.

categories.name: lncRNA
categories.definition: Long noncoding RNA.

categories.name: rRNA
categories.definition: Ribosomal RNA.

categories.name: tRNA
categories.definition: Transfer RNA.

categories.name: Ribozymes
categories.definition: Catalytic RNA.

categories.name: Aptamers
categories.definition: Nucleic-acid binding constructs.

categories.name: Mature / reporter mRNA
categories.definition: Mature transcript or reporter sequence as input/construct; does not imply reconstruction of a transcript from genomic DNA.

categories.name: Promoters
categories.definition: Promoter sequence or promoter annotation.

categories.name: Enhancers
categories.definition: Enhancer sequence or enhancer annotation.

categories.name: Regulatory DNA
categories.definition: Regulatory intervals without a narrower universal element assignment.

categories.name: TF binding sites
categories.definition: Transcription-factor binding motifs or intervals.

categories.name: Polyadenylation sites
categories.definition: Polyadenylation sites or associated signal regions.

categories.name: Terminators
categories.definition: Transcription termination regions or experimental terminator constructs.

categories.name: Biosynthetic gene clusters
categories.definition: Multi-gene biosynthetic clusters.

categories.name: Operons
categories.definition: Co-transcribed bacterial gene groups or boundaries.

categories.name: Repeats / transposable elements
categories.definition: Repeated sequence or transposable-element annotations.

categories.name: Broad genomic sequence
categories.definition: Whole-genome or broadly sampled sequence context; does not imply genome-wide validation or coverage of every element.

categories.name: Intergenic DNA
categories.definition: Sequence between annotated genes.

categories.name: Chromatin boundaries
categories.definition: TAD/insulation boundaries and associated genomic intervals.

categories.name: Embedding analysis
categories.definition: Analyze sequence representations using projection, clustering or similarity diagnostics.
categories.accommodation: Requires access to hidden representations; diagnostic geometry need not measure prediction accuracy.

categories.name: Model interpretability
categories.definition: Relate learned hidden features to genomic annotations.
categories.accommodation: Requires token-level activations and a feature/readout analysis; threshold selection is part of the protocol.

categories.name: Microbiome analysis
categories.definition: Analyze microbial communities, sample structure and associations with host phenotype.

categories.name: Translation initiation site
categories.definition: Translation start codon and its genomic context.

categories.name: Translation termination site
categories.definition: Translation stop codon and its genomic context.

categories.name: Unconditional generation
categories.definition: Sample sequence without a biological prefix, target activity or other example-specific inference condition. Task-specific training can still define the model distribution.
categories.accommodation: A generative sampling procedure is required; a start-of-sequence token alone is not a biological condition.

categories.name: Isolated labels / values
categories.definition: A label, scalar or non-positional vector for a supplied sequence, locus, exon or variant. Multiple tissues/classes do not make a genomic position axis.

categories.name: Sampled position labels
categories.definition: Labels or feature alignment evaluated at selected genomic/token positions. Dense display tracks alone do not establish contiguous held-out scoring.

categories.name: Dense labeling
categories.definition: Biological labels evaluated at successive positions across each assessed sequence. Independent base accuracy does not establish valid exon chains.

categories.name: Signal profiles
categories.definition: Quantitative experimental signal indexed by multiple genomic positions or bins across an assessed sequence. Distinct from annotation labels and one pooled interval value.

categories.name: Element / boundary detection
categories.definition: A set of intervals or boundaries scored by coordinate matching. Correct individual elements do not imply a complete valid gene/transcript.

categories.name: Gene / transcript structures
categories.definition: Linked exon, intron or coding structures evaluated jointly. Coding phase, outer boundaries, isoform multiplicity and matching tolerance remain protocol-specific.

categories.name: Pairwise relationships
categories.definition: A supplied pair, edge or condition contrast is scored. Junction or enhancer–gene scores do not themselves reconstruct a complete graph or transcript.

categories.name: Sequence generation / recovery
categories.definition: Nucleotide identities or generated sequence. This output alone is not biological dense annotation; experimental and computational validation differ.

categories.name: Retrieval / selection
categories.definition: Ranking, retrieving or selecting among supplied candidates, including edits. Candidate choice is not new sequence generation.

categories.name: Aggregate / diagnostic analysis
categories.definition: Representation, constraint, enrichment, interpretation, runtime or cohort-level analysis. Positional visualizations are not automatically annotation benchmarks.

categories.name: Transcript structures
categories.definition: Linked spliced transcript or coding-transcript coordinates. Coverage does not imply alternate-isoform recall, abundance, TSS/TES accuracy or UTR inclusion.

categories.name: Splice junctions
categories.definition: Donor–acceptor connections or intron chains; distinct from independent splice-site identity and from complete transcript recovery.

categories.name: Gene / transcript structure prediction
categories.definition: Predict linked gene/transcript coordinates and evaluate the chain or gene jointly; matching scope and tolerance are stated separately.
categories.accommodation: Structured decoding, phase/strand constraints or a splice graph may be required; independent site labels are insufficient.

categories.name: Signal-profile prediction
categories.definition: Predict quantitative signal indexed by genomic positions or bins; a scalar whole-window count is not a signal profile.
categories.accommodation: Position-preserving features and a quantitative track head; binning and central cropping must be retained.

categories.name: Element / boundary detection
categories.definition: Locate a set of genomic elements or boundaries across an assessed sequence, rather than classify only supplied candidates.
categories.accommodation: Position-preserving features or coordinate outputs; exact/tolerant interval matching is explicit.

categories.name: Contact map
categories.definition: A two-dimensional array of genomic contact values over locus pairs; distinct from a scalar label for a supplied pair.

categories.name: UTRs (unspecified)
categories.definition: Source evaluates an undivided UTR label and does not distinguish 5′ from 3′ UTRs.

categories.name: CRISPR arrays
categories.definition: CRISPR repeat–spacer arrays. Repeat identity and spacer identity are distinct component targets; no complete adaptive-immune-system function is implied.

categories.name: Prophage regions
categories.definition: Integrated bacteriophage regions explicitly supplied or labelled by the task source. Not synonymous with repetitive DNA.

protocols.name: Original Evo 2 variant likelihood scoring
protocols.model_interface: Mutant-minus-reference autoregressive sequence log likelihood
protocols.fitted_component: No additional component fitted for this evaluation; use the cited pretrained/post-trained model or native score.
protocols.split_rule: ClinVar labels define external evaluation cohorts, stratified by coding/noncoding, SNV/non-SNV, phyloP conservation and splice-site proximity. No downstream classifier is fitted.
protocols.notes: Review stars ≥2; both alleles ≤64 nt; VUS removed. Coding is defined using matched RefSeq transcript IDs and GRCh38.p14 annotation. Donor ≤3 bp and acceptor ≤5 bp define proximal variants. A separate arm requires max(SpliceAI,Pangolin) <0.1.

protocols.name: Original Evo 2 position-held-out BRCA1 ridge probe
protocols.model_interface: Four concatenated WT/alternate × forward/reverse pooled embedding views
protocols.fitted_component: Ridge regression; alpha 1,000
protocols.selection: Layer 20; mean-pooling width 128; training-only five-fold grouped cross-validation.
protocols.split_rule: Random split at genomic positions; 1,060 train positions and 266 test positions. Five-fold grouped CV only within training selects layer, pooling width and ridge penalty.

protocols.name: Original Evo 2 species-partitioned midpoint MLP
protocols.model_interface: Concatenated final-position embeddings from two 8,192-bp strand-oriented views; combined span 16,383 bp
protocols.fitted_component: One hidden layer, width 1,024; Evo 2 7B base block 26; Adam, weighted binary cross-entropy
protocols.selection: Validation-species layer selection followed by TPE head tuning on 150 sampled positions/species; final 1,500 positions/species.
protocols.split_rule: Initial random species partition 80/10/10; human, mouse and zebrafish manually assigned to test; two test species excluded for sparse intron labels. Final test panel: eight named species.
protocols.notes: Learning rate 5e-5, batch 16, weight decay 2e-4. Native dense baselines are reduced to the same midpoint label; this does not assess their full structure output.

protocols.selection: Fivefold cross-validation within the 75% training subjects, optimizing negative mean squared error.

protocols.name: DART LoRA fine-tuning
protocols.model_interface: DNA sequence through adapted encoder and task head
protocols.fitted_component: LoRA on linear/convolutional layers; rank 8, alpha 16, dropout 0.05; trained classifier
protocols.selection: Lowest validation loss; AdamW learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 0.01
protocols.split_rule: Trained readout: validation chr 6/21, test chr 5/10/14/18/20/22, remaining chromosomes train; checkpoint minimizing validation loss. This partitions reference sequence-to-activity/classifier training; fixed zero-shot motif/QTL cohorts do not inherit those training partitions.
protocols.notes: Frozen probe; separate LoRA recipe is a linked protocol. Reference sequence targets are used for training.

protocols.name: DART frozen-embedding cell clustering
protocols.model_interface: Mean final-layer sequence embedding; BPE token mean weighted by nucleotide span

protocols.selection: 100 clustering runs; cell labels do not train feature extractor or define bag-of-motif variance selection.
protocols.split_rule: Top 5000 differential peaks per cell line, 25000 total; same fixed cohort clustered and compared with reference cell labels, not a supervised train/test task.
protocols.notes: Distinct from the five-way supervised readout.

protocols.name: BacBench PPI cosine baseline
protocols.model_interface: Pooled sequence / genome embeddings
protocols.fitted_component: None
protocols.selection: Fixed 0.6 STRING threshold; 6000 proteins/2 million pair default caps.
protocols.split_rule: Use embedded genus-held-out split labels. Small release card declares 159 train/49 validation/53 test genomes; published percentage 60/10/20 sums 90 and does not match actual declared rows. No raw pair recount claimed.
protocols.notes: Source scorer reviewed; LOAM readout is a separate fixed sklearn protocol and does not inherit BacBench training defaults.

protocols.name: Current public 12-gene completion implementation
protocols.model_interface: 30% reference prefix; prokaryotic translation/global alignment or eukaryotic exonerate protein2genome alignment
protocols.split_rule: Twelve fixed reference genes; no supervised train/test split. CLI default 50 samples per gene; checked per-gene files use variable sample counts.
protocols.fitted_component: No additional component fitted for this evaluation; use the cited pretrained/post-trained model or native score.
protocols.selection: Temperature 0.7 prokaryote/1.0 eukaryote, top-k 4; ~30% prefix.
protocols.notes: Prokaryotic denominator counts aligned nongap columns after the prompted reference residues. Eukaryotic scorer uses positional identity over the shorter aligned protein suffix, after reference-guided splicing. This is reference recovery, not independent gene-structure annotation.

protocols.name: Original Evo 2 DART allelic embedding comparison
protocols.model_interface: Reference/alternate Evo 2 sequence representations
protocols.split_rule: Fixed QTL cohort; no QTL-label-trained classifier. Block 13 is randomly selected; alternatives were selected externally by BRCA1 training/CV.
protocols.fitted_component: No additional component fitted for this evaluation; use the cited pretrained/post-trained model or native score.
protocols.selection: Block 13 in both sizes; BRCA1-selected block 27 in 7B and block 20 in 40B.
protocols.notes: The original source identifies layers but not exact Evo-specific allele pooling/distance. No generic DART encoder implementation is assumed identical.

protocols.model_interface: 1,048,576-bp DNA plus biological condition → source-defined model readout

protocols.selection: Model/scorer selection uses the source-designated validation axis; final test labels are not used for this selection.
protocols.notes: Exact retained genes/peaks and comparison-group membership require the separate referenced Supplementary Table 8, which was not retrieved.

protocols.selection: One epoch; three seeds; uniform/random pool initialization, pooling-rate multipliers 1/10/100 and reverse-complement input controls are separate conditions. Input contexts extend to 128,000 bp.

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.definition: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

metrics.name: Average precision
metrics.definition: Average precision as implemented by the cited scorer; distinguish from trapezoidal PR area.

metrics.name: AUPRC
metrics.definition: Area under the precision–recall curve; integration convention follows the source.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of correctly classified or recovered targets.

metrics.name: Balanced accuracy
metrics.definition: Mean recall across classes.

metrics.name: MCC
metrics.definition: Matthews correlation coefficient.

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: Harmonic mean of precision and recall; aggregation follows the protocol.

metrics.name: Pearson correlation
metrics.definition: Linear association with measured targets.

metrics.name: Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: Rank association with measured targets.

metrics.name: Absolute Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: Absolute rank correlation; sign is discarded.

metrics.name: MSE
metrics.definition: Mean squared prediction error.

metrics.name: R²
metrics.definition: Coefficient of determination.

metrics.name: Recall@10
metrics.definition: Fraction of queries with a relevant item among ten retrieved candidates.

metrics.name: Recall@5
metrics.definition: Recall among five retrieved candidates.

metrics.name: MAP@5
metrics.definition: Mean average precision at rank five.

metrics.name: V-measure
metrics.definition: Homogeneity/completeness score for clustering.

metrics.name: Bits per base
metrics.definition: Base-normalized negative log probability.

metrics.name: Rank percentile
metrics.definition: Rank of a selected candidate among experimentally measured alternatives.

metrics.name: Selection utility
metrics.definition: Task-specific utility of selected measured sequences.

metrics.name: Enrichment
metrics.definition: Ratio/enrichment defined by the cited population-genetic analysis.

metrics.name: Association discoveries
metrics.definition: Significant gene–phenotype associations under the declared multiplicity correction.

metrics.name: Exact match
metrics.definition: Fraction of targets recovered exactly.

metrics.name: NDCG
metrics.definition: Normalized discounted cumulative gain.

metrics.name: Recall@50
metrics.definition: Recall among fifty retrieved candidates.

metrics.name: Recall AUC
metrics.definition: Area under the causal-SNP recall curve; source defines rank/threshold axis.

metrics.name: Jensen–Shannon distance
metrics.definition: Distance between predicted and observed profile distributions.

metrics.name: Normalized profile improvement
metrics.definition: Clipped improvement of profile Jensen–Shannon distance over a uniform profile.

metrics.name: Runtime
metrics.definition: Elapsed inference or evaluation time under a fixed workload.

metrics.name: Cluster assignment agreement
metrics.definition: Fraction of samples whose low-depth cluster assignment agrees with the full-depth reference; cluster-label correspondence must be specified separately.

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.definition: Fraction of predicted positive features matching the reference.

metrics.name: Recall / sensitivity
metrics.definition: Fraction of reference positive features recovered.

metrics.name: Mean absolute error
metrics.definition: Mean absolute deviation of predicted continuous targets.

metrics.name: BUSCO completeness
metrics.definition: Percentage of expected lineage orthologs recovered as complete; not annotation coordinate accuracy.

metrics.name: max(AUROC, 1 − AUROC)
metrics.definition: Direction-invariant AUROC with experimental scores binarized at the assay median; not raw AUROC.

metrics.name: Absolute MCC
metrics.definition: Absolute Matthews correlation after experimental and model scores are independently median-thresholded.

metrics.name: Top-k splice-site accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of true sites recovered among k predictions, with k equal to the known number of true sites; donor/acceptor averaged.

metrics.name: RNA validation rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of eligible selected predictions meeting the specified RNA-seq criteria; not unselected sensitivity.

metrics.name: Score / measured-effect trend
metrics.definition: Source score-bin distributions or controlled score changes; no single independent predictive correlation asserted.

metrics.name: Tissue heterogeneity test
metrics.definition: Source chi-square p-value for observed novel-junction usage heterogeneity; not accuracy of a tissue-specific model.

metrics.name: Generated component validity
metrics.definition: Source-specific proportion/count of generations containing the required annotated components.

metrics.name: Predicted fold confidence
metrics.definition: Distribution of structure-prediction confidence; not experimentally validated folding.

metrics.name: Selected experimental activity
metrics.definition: Source-defined cleavage or transposition readout in selected candidates; not an unbiased generation success rate.

metrics.name: Predicted coding density
metrics.definition: Fraction of sequence called coding by the specified annotation tool; not true label accuracy.

metrics.name: Predicted RNA occurrence
metrics.definition: Counts of RNA features called by tRNAscan-SE/barrnap; not experimentally verified transcripts.

metrics.name: Stratum-adjusted correlation
metrics.definition: Contact-map correlation stratified by genomic separation; implementation and aggregation must be specified.

metrics.name: False-positive rate
metrics.definition: FP / (FP + TN) on an all-negative or mixed cohort.

metrics.name: False-negative rate
metrics.definition: FN / (FN + TP) on an all-positive or mixed cohort.

metrics.name: Mutation Δ likelihood
metrics.definition: Source-defined change in model sequence likelihood after an artificial mutation; aggregation/context/normalization are protocol-specific. No experimental effect-size label is implied.

metrics.name: Standardized mutation Δ likelihood
metrics.definition: Median model likelihood change by tested codon and species, z-score standardized across the seven tested replacement codons.

metrics.name: Categorical-Jacobian retrieval strength
metrics.definition: Mean magnitude of matched-position query-logit changes following needle-token perturbations, as defined in the Evo 2 supplement.

metrics.name: Retrieval-strength threshold success
metrics.definition: Whether categorical-Jacobian retrieval strength reaches the manually selected 0.8 threshold; not sequence exact-match generation accuracy.

metrics.name: Cohen’s d
metrics.definition: Difference of group means divided by pooled standard deviation.

metrics.name: Adjusted mutual information
metrics.definition: Adjusted mutual information between inferred clusters and reference class labels.

metrics.name: Percent amino-acid recovery
metrics.definition: Source-defined identity of generated amino-acid sequence to a reference; alignment and prompted-region exclusion differ between original and current-release protocols.

metrics.name: Predictor ensemble ICC
metrics.definition: Source-reported intraclass correlation across Enformer/Borzoi tracks; measures oracle agreement, not experimental accuracy.

metrics.name: Experimental accessibility pattern
metrics.definition: ATAC-seq coverage, within-design AUROC and cell-line fold-change endpoints on selected integrated constructs, with source-specific normalization.

metrics.name: Empirical p-value
metrics.definition: Tail fraction under the source-defined resampled null; not a predictive-accuracy score.

metrics.name: Pseudo-perplexity
metrics.definition: Exponentiated weighted mean single-position masked negative log likelihood; not autoregressive sequence perplexity.

metrics.name: SAE feature activation response
metrics.definition: Source-defined mean or per-position SAE activation after controlled sequence perturbation; no experimental phenotype target.

metrics.name: Cross-entropy change after feature ablation
metrics.definition: Difference or ratio of next-token cross-entropy after setting a selected SAE latent to zero and reconstructing the backbone activation; not biological effect size.

metrics.name: Allele log-odds shift
metrics.definition: ALT/REF log odds in ALT carrier background minus ALT/REF log odds in REF carrier background, in bits.

metrics.name: Protein identity recovery
metrics.definition: Fraction of reference proteins with a same-strand overlapping prediction meeting the source-defined global identity threshold.

metrics.name: Valid ORF fraction
metrics.definition: Fraction of predicted coding proteins beginning with methionine and lacking internal stops; syntactic diagnostic, not functional validation.

metrics.name: BUSCO completeness
metrics.definition: Complete single-copy plus duplicated conserved markers as a fraction of the specified BUSCO lineage panel.

metrics.name: Seconds per Mb
metrics.definition: End-to-end annotation wall-clock seconds divided by assembly size; hardware and timing boundary must be stated.

metrics.name: Precision at 70% recall
metrics.definition: Precision at the source operating point attaining 70% recall.

metrics.name: Jensen–Shannon divergence
metrics.definition: Jensen–Shannon divergence in bits between source-defined pooled distributions; distinct from its square-root distance.

metrics.name: Generated/native sequence separability
metrics.definition: Out-of-fold auROC of a generated/native sequence classifier, interpreted with native/native and native/dinucleotide-shuffle controls at the same pool size.

metrics.name: Promoter specificity
metrics.definition: Geometric mean target-to-alternative reporter activity fold change, with confidence limits calculated in log2 space.

metrics.name: Cosine similarity
metrics.definition: Cosine of the angle between the two source-defined vector outputs.

metrics.name: One minus Jensen–Shannon divergence
metrics.definition: One minus base-2 Jensen–Shannon divergence between specified normalized attention profiles.

metrics.name: Motif-group seqlet fraction
metrics.definition: Fraction of activating TF-MoDISco enhancer seqlets assigned to each source-defined motif family; descriptive composition, not motif-recognition accuracy.

metrics.name: Mean log2 fold change
metrics.definition: Mean source-defined log2 response over the specified positions and experimental or shuffled replicates.

metrics.name: Sign accuracy–recall AUC
metrics.definition: Area under cumulative effect-direction accuracy versus fraction of examples retained after ranking by predicted absolute effect magnitude.

findings.description: A.3.6 calls the viral panel 18 DMS datasets, but its prose enumerates more entries and repeats an HIV-envelope author. Individual viral task identities require the released manifest; no exact viral task count is asserted here.
Original Evo 2 usage is restricted to DART 1, 2 and 5. Registering DART does not establish that Evo 2 ran tasks 3 or 4.
The code pins HF data revision 0c1dda471ad13c6126c2cd00cb3fa34852e70673. The HF repository head inspected separately is newer; download revision and repository head must remain distinct.
LOAM’s layer-sweep chooses the best layer on the test set. Its score is a retrospective maximum and should be kept separate from the fixed-last-layer result.
A-domain labels combine experimental evidence, structure-derived inference, homology and sequence predictions. Do not describe all substrate labels as experimental.
The card calls this multi-label, but the pinned Parquet contains one scalar integer label per row in {0,1,2}. The released task is represented as multiclass; the terminology discrepancy is retained.
The LOAM EC test set has one example per class and layer selection maximizes test macro-F1. Treat its layer-sweep as a different protocol from a fixed readout.
All 70 fitness assay files are now inspected; RNA secondary/tertiary structure tasks remain separate and have not been expanded. Fitness count must not be used as a structure benchmark count.
NABench metadata includes a BRCA1 coding assay labeled as enhancer. Functional-region assignments require source study/artifact reconciliation before importing the manifest wholesale.

The card groups eight task families; donor/acceptor targets are separate records here. Promoter/terminator leaf and protoplast measurements are conditions, not separate species. Rice accessions likewise must not inflate species counts.

Current source catalogue contains 23 dataset names. This catalogue splits the paired reporter half-life/ribosome-load targets, yielding 24 task records; cell/RBP/condition columns remain variants.
Evo 2 is compared in v2 training-free recovery, variant scoring and embedding diagnostics; it is explicitly excluded from revised-NT fine-tuning. No Evo 2 fine-tuning use is recorded.

The released GENERator script applies shuffled KFold within training data when it needs validation; it does not automatically rebuild the released test split. Paper ten-fold averages and release chromosome-held-out tests must be distinguished.

The 33 Table S5 subtasks include allele/consequence strata and composite fitness panels. This catalogue has not expanded every constituent assay. RegMix uses selected VEP evaluations during mixture development.

BOTANIC-1’s development aggregate uses 22 scalars in nine families. Twelve additional cross-species site metrics remain reported separately; task/condition scalars must not be counted as independent biological datasets.

NTv3 native C.1 lists 16,262 tracks; C.5 reports 16,260 unique results, omitting one rice and one maize histone track. The standardized benchmark has 155 tracks in 11 species; Evo 2 is independently fine-tuned only in five. Original and external model evaluations remain distinct.
Main-text DeepD methods expose broad endpoints but not all underlying assay IDs and split construction. Composite panels are explicitly marked; they are not counted as fully decomposed benchmarks.
GPN-Star is alignment-conditioned and uses species-specific trained models. Its six-species results must not be represented as a single model transferring to six unseen species.
The LDLR dependency-map analysis is recorded as an exploratory local case study; it does not establish performance on a general experimental genetic-interaction benchmark.

AIDO.DNA2 uses 524-kb coverage inputs and reports 7,379 tracks. The available report does not provide a complete scored track manifest, specify all output bins, or explicitly name the reported correlation as Pearson/Spearman. Long input and local attention do not establish dependence on every distal base.

Genos-m documentation reports 51 genomes and 169,408 genes with 30/10/11 genomes, while the pinned HF artifact inspected for LOAM has 55 genomes and 37/9/9. Release/cohort equivalence has not been established.
Documented 8:2 split conflicts with ~14.5k/1.6k counts (~9:1). Neither is silently converted to exact split counts.

Genos-m Table 9 names checkpoint cpt32k and also gives 1M maximum context. Neither the paper nor released benchmark documentation connects that checkpoint to the final weights or supplies per-model BGC truncation/windowing settings. The reported 1M inference capability does not specify this benchmark protocol.

Genos-m microbiome applications use sample-level host metadata and additional pooling or abundance-model training. They do not establish microbial species holdouts, direct host-DNA prediction or cross-chunk genomic dependency learning.

The pinned five-fold split file has 2,315 rows (463/fold), while the domain-instance table has 2,504 rows. The scorer further restricts labels/classes; split-file rows must not be presented as final scored single-label instances.

Methods state 36,668TIS sites(26,653/10,015), whereasTable 1/H Fcard state 36,662(26,650/10,012). Non-TIS methods 183,687 versus card 183,685 also differ. Preserve reported counts and inspected artifact counts separately.

The linked leaderboard has 20 species-specific entries corresponding to 12 dataset/target configurations. Its mean percentile ranking combines different contexts and selected Evo 2 orientations. PlantCAD2.5-L is labeled under development; that label does not establish a public model release.
PaperTable 2 summarizes mean AUPRC across 92 cell types, while results prose and released scorer use micro-averaged precision-recall/average precision. These aggregations must remain distinct.

GeneCAD 2025 preprint uses five species and frozen 88M/large PlantCAD2 encoders. The 2026 release uses eight species and explicitly updates a 200M PlantCAD2-family backbone. Its core benchmark is CDS-only with both default and strict gffcompare scoring; those scores must not be presented as full UTR/transcript annotation accuracy.

The inspected release manifest lists 213 prediction files with declared hashes and prediction counts. Reference annotations are linked to their original sources and are not redistributed. Declared hashes were not independently verified against every GFF file.

Translation train and validation files both contain Arabidopsis chromosomes 1–5; test contains maize chromosomes 1–10. This is species-transfer testing with validation on shared chromosomes. No gene-level validation-selection rule is supplied by the paper or released preparation code.

The paper describes log10-transformed translation abundance. Every released regression label in train, validation and test instead matches log10(1 + TPM), with maximum absolute error below 7e-15. The catalogue uses the released transformation and retains the paper statement separately.

Translation train and validation files both contain Arabidopsis chromosomes 1–5; test contains maize chromosomes 1–10. This is species-transfer testing with validation on shared chromosomes. No gene-level validation-selection rule is supplied by the paper or released preparation code.

GUE is version-dependent: the supplied list describes an original 28-dataset/7-category suite, whereas DNABERT-2 arXiv v2 describes 36 datasets across 9 tasks. Existing selective GUE records are retained; neither headline count is treated as complete artifact-audited coverage.

Gene-MTEB README says four clustering tasks in its overview but lists four human-virus and four HMP clustering entries; METAGENE-1 section 5.3 describes eight. Reconcile implementation and actual datasets before task expansion.
