Paper Table 1 reports 5,976 instances and 4,780/597/597 train/validation/test (sum 5,974). Release has 5,977 BED rows: 4,783 train, 597 valid, 597 test, with 5,974 distinct transcript IDs and three duplicate IDs confined to train. All 5,977 HDF5 label vectors match BED spans of 1,433–13,000 bp; the pinned embedding config adds no extra flanks. The paper reports up to 14,000 bp. Historical paper-time input artifacts are not identified by a release checksum, so reported and measured ranges/counts remain distinct.

The image shows five points, one labelled for each assay family with its track count. The surrounding report and figure legend describe each point as a track. This is not a released per-track prediction/score table; aggregation across tracks is not specified.

Supplement reports 470 positive source SNVs before processing. Pinned released benchmark contains 433 positive and 503,959 control rows. These are distinct filtering stages; the positive source count is not the released cohort size.

Supplement A.3.4 names the diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana as ciliate-code, whereas main Fig. 2e names Paramecium tetraurelia. NCBI assigns T. pseudonana standard nuclear code 1, and Paramecium/Tetrahymena ciliate nuclear code 6. Both source identity claims remain explicit; the supplement’s label is not used as taxonomy.

Pinned MIBiG DNA splits share one exact Sequence string; protein splits share 279 distinct exact protein Sequence strings. BGC Entry identifiers remain distinct targets and protein vectors are pooled within Entry. Exact-string recurrence is not a full homology or pretraining audit.

The FeFe sequence table has 429 rows but only 384 unique Entry IDs; 45 repeated IDs all have identical sequences. Its 73,536 distance rows equal 384 choose 2. The evaluator selects the final sequence row for each ID, so 429 must not be reported as the number of tree leaves.

Both pinned retrieval qrels repositories include train relevance-pair tables and test query-sequence tables. The pinned evaluator maps qrels_dict_init over the full Dataset Dict, although the test split lacks query_id, corpus_id and fuzz_ratio. This source code/data interface conflict is retained explicitly.

GPRA assay randomization spans 80 bases, but released seq values are 110 nt because 30 nt of scaffold are included. Previous 80 bp input description conflated randomized region with released model input.

The general scoring guide says most test labels are private, but pinned ClinVar test includes public y labels and 11,964 rows. It has no training set and uses source/date cohort separation, not a chromosome holdout.

DART compares only ChromBPNet’s total-count head to DNALMs, not its base-level profile head. Quantitative QTL effects are counterfactual outputs of DNase-trained sequence-to-activity models, not directly QTL-trained probes.

Pinned phenotype code defaults to genus grouped 70/10/20, whereas task README describes random as the default. Labels supply genus, so the random fallback is not the default intended protocol. Actual group failure fallback still requires run provenance.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Post-hoc latent-feature annotation alignment statistic
task_outputs.scoring_unit: Source-defined one-versus-rest Domain F1 on the annotated E. coli reference
task_outputs.rationale: SAE trains on approximately 305,000 random 32k pretraining chunks, token activations downsampled 10-fold and globally shuffled to approximately 1 billion. 4,096 latents, Batch-TopK 128, batch 4096, LR 5e-5, one epoch. Feature search on E. coli NC000913.3 ORF/intergenic/tRNA/rRNA annotations; one-versus-rest Domain F1 after activation-threshold sweeping. The source gives no Domain F1 formula, threshold grid, complete feature-selection rule, label arrays, candidate token count or separate feature-search validation/test split.
task_outputs.limitations: Feature/threshold search and evaluation reuse the annotated genome. Exact formula, denominator and scorer are not provided; no held-out dense annotation claim.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Aggregate response of model likelihood/logits to source-defined perturbations
task_outputs.scoring_unit: Relative gene-boundary position; mean across alternate alleles and sampled genes
task_outputs.rationale: Twenty prokaryotic and sixteen eukaryotic references. Randomly select 1,024 coding genes/species except Nanoarchaeum equitans (all 536). Mutate every position from 20 bp upstream to 20 bp downstream of the start-codon first base to all three alternate bases. Evo 2 7B scores 8,192 nt contexts centered on the mutation, averaging original/reverse-complement likelihoods. Average delta likelihood over alternate bases and genes at each relative position. Repeat around stop codons. These profiles have no experimental mutation-effect labels.
task_outputs.limitations: The statistical endpoint is explicit. Missing processed score/coordinate artifacts remain source limits; no prediction-label accuracy is invented.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Aggregate response of model likelihood/logits to source-defined perturbations
task_outputs.rationale: Twenty named bacterial/archaeal reference assemblies. Per species sample 5,000 CDS positions and 2,000 positions each from rRNA, tRNA, ncRNA and non-annotated/intergenic bases. CDS: three alternate SNVs and 1 bp deletion; noncoding groups:10 bp deletion. Extend flanks after deletion to preserve 8,192 bp context. Use standard codon table for synonymous/missense/nonsense grouping. Compare likelihood changes, not experimental fitness. The main Figure 2 caption identifies Evo 2 7B; the supplement abbreviates this as Evo 7B.
task_outputs.limitations: The statistical endpoint is explicit. Missing processed score/coordinate artifacts remain source limits; no prediction-label accuracy is invented.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Aggregate response of model likelihood/logits to source-defined perturbations
task_outputs.scoring_unit: Median mutation likelihood per region/mutation type, then species-level comparison
task_outputs.rationale: Sixteen named eukaryotic assemblies. Artificial synonymous/nonsynonymous/premature-stop substitutions and 1 bp CDS frameshift deletions;10 bp deletions in UTRs, introns, intergenic regions and annotated noncoding RNA exons. Species-specific codon tables. Keep 8,192 bp context by extending deletion flanks. Sample up to 200,000 sequences across types and at most 20 mutations per unique region coordinate; summarize median likelihood change by region/mutation type. Primary Figure 2d uses 7B; Extended Data Fig. 3c compares 40B versus 7B across the plotted coding and noncoding classes on the same sequences. Exact per-species/type retained counts are not reported.
task_outputs.limitations: The statistical endpoint is explicit. Missing processed score/coordinate artifacts remain source limits; no prediction-label accuracy is invented.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Aggregate response of model likelihood/logits to source-defined perturbations
task_outputs.scoring_unit: Tested replacement codon within species and context/recoding condition
task_outputs.rationale: Supplement lists five species and tests seven replacement codons (TAA, TAG, TGA, AGG, TCA, AGA, TTA), which are not all stop codons under each genetic code. Random CDS/codon positions, pseudogenes excluded; source minimum length threshold 10 and maximum 200,000 sequences/genome. Evo 2 7B contexts 100–8,192 bp; median mutation likelihood changes per codon/species, z-standardized across seven codons. Ciliate recoding replaces TAA/TAG glutamine codons with randomly selected standard glutamine codons. Supplement names Thalassiosira pseudonana as ciliate-code; main Figure 2e instead identifies Paramecium tetraurelia. This taxon/code discrepancy is retained explicitly.
task_outputs.limitations: The statistical endpoint is explicit. Missing processed score/coordinate artifacts remain source limits; no prediction-label accuracy is invented.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Aggregate response of model likelihood/logits to source-defined perturbations
task_outputs.scoring_unit: Gene-relative codon position; higher/lower-tAI mutation group; rolling five-codon average
task_outputs.rationale: Four named species: human, yeast, Aeropyrum pernix, E. coli. Use previously calculated tRNA-adaptation-index values to separate synonymous substitutions into increased versus decreased tAI. Average model log-likelihood changes across sampled genes/codon positions; rolling five-codon smoothing. Main Extended Data Fig. 3d additionally depicts tAI along first/last 100 codons after z-normalization. tAI is a genomic/codon-usage proxy, not an experimental protein-fitness target. Exact sampled gene/mutation counts and checkpoint size are not specified in this section.
task_outputs.limitations: The statistical endpoint is explicit. Missing processed score/coordinate artifacts remain source limits; no prediction-label accuracy is invented.

task_outputs.prediction_form: Aggregate response of model likelihood/logits to source-defined perturbations
task_outputs.scoring_unit: Synthetic needle/haystack context and needle depth; shuffled-pattern null separately
task_outputs.rationale: Uniform-random 100 bp needle and DNA haystack; haystack lengths 512–1,048,576 bp in powers of two. Insert needle at 10–90% context depths by 10% increments and exact query copy at suffix. Retrieval strength is mean matching-position categorical-Jacobian magnitude across 100 needle/query positions; success threshold r ≥ 0.8 chosen by manual inspection. Null validation: eight lengths 512–65,536, ten depths 10–100%, 13 independent shuffles, 1,040 scores; maximum 0.037 and reported P < 0.001 at 0.8. This is a perturbation-based repeated-pattern diagnostic on synthetic DNA, not natural-genome retrieval accuracy.
task_outputs.limitations: The statistical endpoint is explicit. Missing processed score/coordinate artifacts remain source limits; no prediction-label accuracy is invented.

data_resources.title: Experimental chromatin-design sequences
data_resources.notes: Workbook contains six mouse design sequences (five 19,968-nt sequences and one 19,584-nt sequence), 50 human construct rows plus the pAF0977 plasmid. Human rows comprise 43 short constructs (including three named controls) and seven long constructs. A11 and B1 have identical sequence strings; C6 contains one nonbreaking-space character. Two raw-read construct IDs, E1 and E4, are absent. Human synthesis strings generally include 40 flanking bases in addition to 1,024/4,096 designed bases.

Clustering scorer inserts integer -1 for missing taxonomy depths, then converts mixed string/integer labels to a NumPy array. The sentinel becomes string -1 and the subsequent comparison against integer -1 retains it. Missing depths can therefore form a scored class. This behavior was reproduced with the same NumPy conversion/comparison, without rerunning model inference.

Supplement explicitly defines 31 human ProteinGym v0.1 assays, single-nucleotide-accessible amino-acid substitutions and CADD-based nucleotide choice. Complete current/archived GPN code and official HF registry do not release a GPN-Star-specific assay/retained-variant manifest. The upstream GPN-MSA 31-item list is identifiable but is not asserted to equal the final GPN-Star scored intersection.

Supplement defines curated regulatory positives and nine matched common controls per positive. Exact matched cohort, processed score tables and retained all-model intersection are not present in the inspected official registry/release.

The original study measures relative ligation activity in the 35 nt catalytic core of the F1*U RNA ligase, including evolutionary trajectory libraries and the 2^16 intermediates between two active sequences. It is not a hammerhead self-cleavage assay. The study-wide total over 120,000 sequences is not substituted for the counts of individual NABench files.

The devices use ligand-responsive aptamer–ribozyme tertiary interactions, measured by FACS-Seq in budding yeast W303α. They are not mammalian toehold switches. The synthetic device sequences are distinguished from the assay host; linker lengths remain variants of the same device-activity task.

A library of 6,500 designed promoters tests yeast transcription-factor sites and nucleosome-disfavoring sequences through YFP expression and cell sorting. E. coli is used for plasmid amplification before transformation into yeast. The study is not an HEK293 promoter assay. The two NABench files are release-specific variants, not independent human assays.

The study synthesizes 13,000 oligos encoding 7,536 unique 118 bp core-promoter sequences, with extra barcoded replicates, and measures reporter activity in S. cerevisiae. It includes native, designed and orthologous promoters. NABench does not release this processed file; neither the study total nor a generic ADH1 library description establishes its retained NABench cohort.

split_strategies.name: Random rows or variants
split_strategies.description: Assign examples randomly, possibly stratifying labels.
split_strategies.protection: Separates recorded examples and estimates performance on similar sampled examples.
split_strategies.limitations: Identical strings, nearby loci, repeated donors, mutation positions and gene families can cross partitions.

split_strategies.name: Chromosome holdout
split_strategies.description: Reserve whole named chromosomes for validation or test.
split_strategies.protection: Separates loci on the reference assembly when assignment is applied to the actual input span.
split_strategies.limitations: Repeats, paralogs and homologous chromosomes/species can retain related DNA. Label holdout is distinct from sequence-model training exclusion.

split_strategies.name: Genomic blocks
split_strategies.description: Assign larger genomic intervals, with any source-defined padding or buffers.
split_strategies.protection: Can separate nearby windows and long-range labels when windows and buffers respect the boundary.
split_strategies.limitations: Disjoint block IDs or scored cores do not establish that full extended input windows are disjoint.

split_strategies.name: Genes or homology groups
split_strategies.description: Group related transcripts, genes or proteins before partitioning.
split_strategies.protection: Can reduce leakage through isoforms or homologs at the supplied grouping threshold.
split_strategies.limitations: Unmapped genes, grouping thresholds and overlapping genomic spans require separate checks.

split_strategies.name: Sequence similarity
split_strategies.description: Separate examples using sequence similarity, clustering or a similarity-reduction objective.
split_strategies.protection: Reduces related inputs across partitions according to the stated algorithm.
split_strategies.limitations: A swap heuristic that lowers average similarity is not a strict identity threshold and can leave exact duplicates.

split_strategies.name: Mutation positions
split_strategies.description: Keep mutations at a position or contiguous position block together.
split_strategies.protection: Reduces reuse of the same mutated position across training and test.
split_strategies.limitations: Background sequences, nearby positions and multi-mutant combinations can still be shared.

split_strategies.name: Species, genera or clades
split_strategies.description: Hold out entire source taxa at an explicitly named rank.
split_strategies.protection: Tests transfer across the held-out taxa rather than random rows from the same taxon.
split_strategies.limitations: Conserved sequences and horizontal transfer cross taxon boundaries. Pretraining taxon exclusion is a separate condition.

split_strategies.name: Individuals or donors
split_strategies.description: Group all measurements from an individual or donor.
split_strategies.protection: Separates participants across the fitted predictor’s train/test data.
split_strategies.limitations: Genes and reference sequences may intentionally be shared. Population structure and related donors can remain.

split_strategies.name: Assay tracks or conditions
split_strategies.description: Mask labels for selected cell types, conditions or assays.
split_strategies.protection: Tests an unobserved measurement context or assay.
split_strategies.limitations: The same reference DNA may have been seen with other labels; track exclusion is not genome exclusion.

split_strategies.name: Time or source version
split_strategies.description: Evaluate observations or datasets released after a named cutoff.
split_strategies.protection: Separates new measurements from earlier training and selection sources.
split_strategies.limitations: The same loci, individuals or similar assays may occur in both periods; validation data can still guide selection.

split_strategies.name: BGCs, gene-cluster families or chemical scaffolds
split_strategies.description: Group biosynthetic clusters or first-product scaffolds before splitting.
split_strategies.protection: Targets transfer across clusters or chemistry at the chosen grouping level.
split_strategies.limitations: Parent-cluster grouping is weaker than GCF grouping. Shared domain sequences may still occur in different clusters.

split_strategies.name: Fixed zero-shot or observational cohort
split_strategies.description: Score a fixed assay or external cohort without fitting a new task-specific predictor.
split_strategies.protection: Defines a common score cohort; there is no downstream fitting split to compare.
split_strategies.limitations: Pretraining, benchmark-driven model selection, scorer tuning and cohort ascertainment still matter. No downstream split is not evidence of no contamination.

split_audits.title: DGEB: MIBiG DNA classification
split_audits.scope: Complete named released files and their source-defined comparison units.
split_audits.method: Complete selected files; exact case-sensitive strings, plus uppercase reverse-complement equivalence for DNA only. No similarity search or pretraining comparison.
split_audits.conclusion: The comparison quantifies the named released separation axis; broader independence is not established.
split_audits.limitations: No local/global alignment, k-mer similarity threshold, biological score reproduction or model-pretraining comparison. Zero observed overlap applies only to the named keys, files and partitions.

split_audits.title: PlantCAD2: maize cell-type accessibility
split_audits.scope: All 3,390,419 released 600-bp core windows: prior complete exact-string counts; complete lightweight coordinate checks; bounded recovery of illustrative rows. This is not a rescan of all long-context model inputs.
split_audits.method: Reuse prior full exact-sequence counts. Read all coordinate columns only for interval checks. Bounded sequence-row pass recovers illustrative matches; it does not estimate or replace full counts.
split_audits.conclusion: Chromosome-10 test separation is supported for the released coordinates. Exact DNA uniqueness across partitions is not met. Training/validation core windows also have positive-length interval overlaps; distinct coordinate IDs did not establish disjoint intervals.
split_audits.limitations: No local/global alignment, k-mer similarity threshold, biological score reproduction or model-pretraining comparison. Zero observed overlap applies only to the named keys, files and partitions. The prior full sequence scan predates this bounded survey. Only 1,258,184 sequence rows were read to retrieve examples. Examples of equal labels do not establish the labels of every recurring string. Counts of shared strings are not counts of affected rows.

split_audits.title: mRNABench: Sugimoto ribosome load, seed 2541
split_audits.scope: Complete named released files and their source-defined comparison units.
split_audits.method: Execute exact pinned train_test_split_homologous function twice, seed 2541, after target null/NaN exclusion; human HomoloGene map. Reconstructed library-default split, not asserted historical paper/embedding cohort.
split_audits.conclusion: The mapped HomoloGene groups are disjoint, while exact sequences and unmapped gene names recur. The source function splits unmapped rows independently, so the grouping rule does not guarantee sequence or gene-name uniqueness.
split_audits.limitations: No local/global alignment, k-mer similarity threshold, biological score reproduction or model-pretraining comparison. Zero observed overlap applies only to the named keys, files and partitions. Reconstructed seed 2541 after target-eligibility filtering, without historical embeddings. Other seeds, model-dependent feature filtering and the original paper’s actual run identities are not reconstructed.

split_audits.title: NTv3: full long-context inputs excluded

split_audits.title: SpliceAI2: split cohort access

split_audits.title: DART-Eval: source split rules, no input recount

split_audits.title: Yeast H3: NT / GUE cross-release partition exposure
